COMPANY PROFILE WATER FIT GENERAL TRADING, a midsized manufacturer, supplier and distributor of water work related products. It competes in mature markets, and its commodity markets have recently undergone significant consolidation. Continually improving its supply chain efficiencies and differentiating its services and products with value-added services have become WATER FIT’s new bases of competition. WATER FIT GENERAL TRADING is supporting its strategy with an integrated systems platform that is also an engine for the company’s long-term growth. The products ranged from water work related tools and equipment, water distribution items (pipes, pumps etc), and water storage equipment, to water treatment chemicals and hygiene and sanitation products, UPVC Pipes & fittings HDPE pipe & fitting, PPR pipe & fitting, Galvanized pipe & fitting, Irrigation line & accessories, Gardening accessories, Water proof membrane, G-Tex membrane for perforated pipes, Industrial Valves & fitting, Butt-Welding installation for HDPE pipes, Suction & delivery hose, Steel & PVC casing. WATER FIT GENERAL TRADING is engaged in manufacturing, wholesale, retail, commission (trade) agency and general supply firm with a reputation for integrity, quality products, craftsmanship, and excellence in management. In recent years annual sales have increased to be well over 35 million Ethiopian Birr. The business has its address in leased premises at Mickyleyland Street, Bole Sub-City, an Addis Ababa, and Ethiopia. WATER FIT GENERAL TRADING is involved in the following activities: Manufacturing of HDPE pipes ,Irrigation Pipes and Single well corrugated pipes Supply of quality products to water supply and irrigation projects Supply of sanitary fittings to Residential & Commercial Construction buildings. Commission agency and distribution Services to manufacturers. Retail Roof and Floor Coverings. Provision of Butt-wielding services. The main objective of the business is to provide quality products, services and all resources towards a smooth and successful completion of projects to appropriate standards. In order to ensure the continues supply of quality products and the rendering of high quality services for client, the business at all stages of product and the service provision process, utilize efficient equipment and technology. The products to be supplied, the equipment to be employed and professionals to be involved to each and every specific water works are all high standard quality, state of the art and well qualified and have rich experience on similar projects executed successfully. With the supply of high quality products, employing highly qualified professionals and energetic supporting staff, we have built a capacity to handle supplies intended to projects in quality, timely and within client’s budget. WATER FIT GENERAL TRADING has successfully manufactured HDPE pipes, Single well corrugated conduit & Drip irrigation pipes supplied materials and equipment to projects which are completed and handed over projects under taken by public and private institution throughout the country. We aim to participate in national and international competitive bids for the procurement of supplies for the projects financed by Federal, Regional government budget, private sector as well as those funded by UN agencies, international or continental monetary agencies, NGOs and donor governments intended to Ethiopia. 1.1 General This manual is prepared for the purpose of defining WATER FIT’s interpretations of the ISO 9001:2015 international standard, as well as to demonstrate how the company complies with that standard. This manual presents “Notes” which are used to define how WATER FIT has tailored its management system to suit its purposes. These are intended to clarify implementation approaches and interpretations for concepts which are not otherwise clearly defined in ISO 9001:2015. Where subordinate or supporting documentation is reference in this manual, these are indicated by their document numbers and titles. TERMS & DEFINITIONS For the purpose of this manual, in addition to the definitions given in ISO 9000:2015, Quality Management System: Fundamentals and Vocabulary, the following definitions shall apply: General Terminology Top Management: Top Management of WATER FIT includes: The General Manager, the Deputy General Managers and Heads of Departments. Document: written information used to describe how an activity is done. Record: captured evidence of an activity having been done. Documented Information: an information that is required to be controlled and maintained by an organization Act: Primary responsibility given to a person or group of persons to accomplish a specific process/activity, which results in a specific output. Audit: Systematic, independent and documented process for obtaining audit evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which audit criteria are fulfilled. Conformity: Fulfillment of a requirement. Customer: Organization or person that receives a product. Customer satisfaction: Customer's perception of the degree to which customer’s requirements has been fulfilled. Concession: Permission to use or release the product that does not conform to specified require. Corrective Action: A step or action taken to correct a deviation or a deficiency. Certification: Action by a third party demonstrating that adequate confidence is given that a duly identified product, process or service conforms with a specific standard or other normative document. Effectiveness: Extent to which planned activities are realized and planned results are achieved. Efficiency: Relationship between the result achieved and the resources used. Management: Coordinated activities to direct and control an organization. Management system: System to establish policy and objectives and to achieve those objectives. Non–conformance: Non fulfillment of specified requirement. Organization: Group of people and facilities with an arrangement of responsibilities, authorities and relationships Organizational structure: Arrangement of responsibilities, authorities and relationships between people. Preventive action: Action to eliminate the cause of a potential nonconformity. Procedure: Specified way to carry out an activity or a process. Process: Set of interrelated or interacting activities which transform inputs to outputs. Product (service): Result of a process. Quality management system: Management system to direct and control an organization with regard to quality. Single well corrugated pipes: pipes with ridges and grooves on the inside and outside. They are often made from high-density polyethylene (HDPE) Drip irrigation pipes: are fundamental components of micro-irrigation systems, designed to deliver water directly to plant roots with high efficiency and it is specialized polyethylene tubing system that transports water from the water source to plant root zones through a network of emitters or built-in drip points. Risk-Based Thinking Terminology Risk – Negative effect of uncertainty Opportunity – Positive effect of uncertainty Uncertainty - A deficiency of information related to understanding or knowledge of an event, its consequence, or likelihood. (Not to be confused with measurement uncertainty.) Nonconforming Product Terminology Rework: Efforts to bring nonconforming product into conformance through additional operations that do not alter the original design of the product. Repair: Efforts to bring nonconforming product into conformance through additional operations that alter the original design of the product; this may be through the addition of material no specified in the original design, or through altering pre-existing design features. Scrap: The discard of nonconforming product in lieu of rework or repair. PLANNING 6.1 Actions to Address Risks and Opportunities 6.1.1 When planning for the Quality Management System, WATER FIT has considered the issues referred to in 4.1 and the requirements referred to in 4.2 and determine the risks and opportunities that need to be addressed to: give assurance that the Quality Management System can achieve its intended result(s); enhance desirable effects; prevent, or reduce, undesired effects; achieve improvement. Note: WATER FIT deviates slightly from the approach towards risk and opportunity presented in ISO 9001. Instead, WATER FIT views “uncertainty” as neutral, but defines “risk” as a negative effect of uncertainty, and “opportunity” as a positive effect of uncertainty. WATER FIT has elected to manage risks and opportunities separately, except where they may overlap. Formal risk management may not be utilized in all instances; instead, the level of risk assessment, analysis, treatment and recordkeeping will be performed to the level deemed appropriate for each circumstance or application. WATER FIT considers risks and opportunities when taking actions within the management system, as well as when implementing or improving the management system; likewise, these are considered relative to products and services. Risks and opportunities are identified as part of the “Context of the Organization Exercise” defined in (OF/WF/031), as well as throughout all other activities of the QMS. 6.1.2 WATER FIT has planned: actions to address these risks and opportunities; how to: integrate and implement the actions into its Quality Management System processes; evaluate the effectiveness of these actions. Actions taken to address risks and opportunities will be proportionate to the potential impact on the conformity of products and services. 6.2 Quality Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them 6.2.1 WATER FIT has established Quality Objectives (OF/WF/027) at relevant functions, levels and processes needed for the quality management system. The quality objectives are: consistent with the quality policy; measurable; take into account applicable requirements; relevant to conformity of products and services and to enhancement of customer satisfaction; monitored; communicated; updated as appropriate. WATER FIT has maintained documented information on the quality objectives. 6.2.2 When planning how to achieve its quality objectives, WATER FIT has determined: what will be done; what resources will be required; who will be responsible; when it will be completed; how the results will be evaluated. 6.3 Planning of Changes When WATER FIT determines the need for changes to the Quality Management System, the changes are carried out in a planned manner. WATER FIT has considered: the purpose of the changes and their potential consequences; the integrity of the quality management system; the availability of resources; the allocation or reallocation of responsibilities and authorities. 7. WATER FIT has dealt with nonconforming outputs in one or more of the following ways: correction; segregation, containment, return or suspension of provision of products and services; informing the customer; obtaining authorization for acceptance under concession. Conformity to the requirements will be verified when nonconforming outputs are corrected. 8.7.2 WATER FIT has retained documented information that: describes the nonconformity; describes the actions taken; describes any concessions obtained; identifies the authority deciding the action in respect of the nonconformity. 9. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION 9.1 Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis and Evaluation 9.1.1 General WATER FIT has determined: what needs to be monitored and measured; the methods for monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation needed to ensure valid results; when the monitoring and measuring shall be performed; when the results from monitoring and measurement shall be analyzed and evaluated. WATER FIT has evaluated the performance and the effectiveness of the Quality Management System and retained appropriate documented information as evidence of the results. 9.1.2 Customer Satisfaction WATER FIT has monitored customers’ perceptions of the degree to which their needs and expectations have been fulfilled and determined the methods for obtaining; monitoring and reviewing this information (See OP/WF/025). 9.1.3 Analysis and Evaluation WATER FIT has analyzed and evaluated appropriate data and information arising from monitoring and measurement (See OP/WF/009). The results of analysis shall be used to evaluate: conformity of products and services; the degree of customer satisfaction; the performance and effectiveness of the quality management system; if planning has been implemented effectively; the effectiveness of actions taken to address risks and opportunities; the performance of external providers; the need for improvements to the quality management system. NOTE: Methods to analyze data can include statistical techniques. 9.2 Internal Audit 9.2.1 WATER FIT has conducted internal audits at least once a year to provide information on whether the Quality Management System: conforms to: the organization’s own requirements for its quality management system; the requirements of this International Standard; is effectively implemented and maintained. 9.2.2 WATER FIT has: planned, established, implemented and maintained an audit program (s) including the frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning requirements and reporting, which shall take into consideration the importance of the processes concerned, changes affecting the organization, and the results of previous audits; defined the audit criteria and scope for each audit; selected auditors and conduct audits to ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process; ensured that the results of the audits are reported to relevant management; taken appropriate correction and corrective actions without undue delay; retained documented information as evidence of the implementation of the audit program and the audit results. (See OP/WF/003). 9.3 Management Review 9.3.1 General Top management of WATER FIT reviewed the organization’s Quality Management System at least once a year to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy, effectiveness and alignment with the strategic direction of the organization (See OP/WF/006). 9.3.2 Management Review Inputs The management review is planned and carried out taking into consideration: the status of actions from previous management reviews; changes in external and internal issues that are relevant to the quality management system; information on the performance and effectiveness of the Quality Management System, including trends in: customer satisfaction and feedback from relevant interested parties; the extent to which quality objectives have been met; process performance and conformity of products and services; nonconformities and corrective actions; monitoring and measurement results; audit results; the performance of external providers; the adequacy of resources; the effectiveness of actions taken to address risks and opportunities (see 6.1); opportunities for improvement. 9.3.3 Management Review Outputs The outputs of the management review include decisions and actions related to: opportunities for improvement; any need for changes to the quality management system; resource needs. WATER FIT has retained documented information as evidence of the results of management reviews. 10. IMPROVEMENT 10.1 General WATER FIT has determined and selected opportunities for improvement and implement any necessary actions to meet customer requirements and enhance customer satisfaction. These include: improving products and services to meet requirements as well as to address future needs and expectations; correcting, preventing or reducing undesired effects; improving the performance and effectiveness of the quality management system. 10.2 Nonconformity and Corrective Action 10.2.1 When nonconformity occurs, including any arising from complaints, WATER FIT has: reacted to the nonconformity and, as applicable: take action to control and correct it; deal with the consequences; evaluated the need for action to eliminate the cause(s) of the nonconformity, in order that it does not recur or occur elsewhere, by: reviewing and analyzing the nonconformity; determining the causes of the nonconformity; determining if similar nonconformities exist, or could potentially occur; implemented any action needed; reviewed the effectiveness of any corrective action taken; updated risks and opportunities determined during planning, if necessary; made changes to the Quality Management System, if necessary. Corrective actions are appropriate to the effects of the nonconformities encountered. 10.2.2 WATER FIT has retained documented information as evidence of: the nature of the nonconformities and any subsequent actions taken; the results of any corrective action. (See OP/WF/004) 10.3 Continual Improvement WATER FIT has continually improved the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the Quality Management System. WATER FIT has considered the results of analysis and evaluation, and the outputs from management review, to determine if there are needs or opportunities that shall be addressed as part of continual improvement. Quality of Work Work is exact, accurate, thorough, and free from errors and the neatness of finished products, work and services are as expected when completed under normal conditions. 4. Cooperation (Attitude, Working with Others, Inter-Personal Relationship) Works effectively with superiors, fellow workers and others. Where applicable, is pleasant in contact with public and/or client. Interests in the job and accepts company policies and practices. 5. Attendance (Punctuality, Dependability) Arrives at work on time and meets other commitments in a timely manner. Overall attendance record and attitude to work are positive. Works well and tasks are undertaken effectively without close supervision. 6. Safety/Confidentiality Follows good safety practices, is aware of own and others’ personal safety. Handles confidential information in accordance with procedures. 7. Initiative (Creativity) Acts on own initiative. Able to analyze situations, problems, assigned duties and organizational needs and able to make decisions and take actions without being told. Ability to foresee the outcome and consequences of decisions and accept accountability. 8. Supervisory Capability Able to delegate work and assign responsibility to subordinates while maintaining adequate control. Has the willingness and desire to work towards common objectives. Able to select, train and motivate personnel to handle difficult works and greater responsibilities. Promotes the development of other individuals. A good teacher and model for others, able to define measurable objectives and set attainable goals. Identifies and pays attention to critical areas. 9. Communication Effective in oral and written communication and able to keep subordinates, associates, superiors and others adequately, clearly and concisely informed. 10. Planning and Organizing Able to effectively plan and organize work. Sets priorities, forecasts needs and budgets time and resources to accomplish jobs. Asks for help when needed and remains aware of project requirements. Skilled in establishing goals, effective actions, using resources, allocating personnel, and time (including own) efficiently. 11. Adaptability Adjusts to new assignments, changing conditions, peak work loads, tight deadlines, new duties and procedures. Is open-minded and willing to accept new ideas. 12. Cost Effectiveness Able to generate and implement cost saving ideas and utilize the most economical methods. Uses feedback to control costs. Flexible and willing to modify plans to meet budget objective. Achieves budget goals. ዘገባዎችን ለበላይ አላፊዎች ያቀርባል፡፡ • በማምረቻው ውስጥ ያሉ የፈረቃ መሪዎች በአግባቡ ኃላፊነታቸውን መወጣታቸውን ይቆጣጠራል፡፡ አስፈላጊ ሆኖ ሲገኝ ኃላፊነታቸውን በማይወጡት ላይ ተገቢውን የማስተካከያ እርምጃ ይወስዳል፡፡ • የፋሪካው የየዕለቱ የፈረቃዎች ወይም የነጠላ ምርት ውጠየቶች በትክክል እንዲመዘገቡና መረጃዎችንም በአግባቡ በቋሚነት እንዲያዙ የሚያስችል ስርዓት ይዘረጋል፡፡ ሰራተኞችም በዚሁ ላይ በቂ ግንዛቤ እንዲኖራቸው ያለማቋረጥ ጥረት ያደርጋል፡፡ • የማምረቻ ሠራተኞች በተገቢው የስራ መደቦቻቸው መደላደላቸውን ዝርዝር የስራ ድርሻ መስጠታቸውን ያረጋግጣል፤ እያንዳንዱ ባሙያ በልምድና በክህሎት እንዲዳብር ይጥራል፡፡ የተለያዩ የማረቻ ዘዴዎችን ተጠቅሞ ምርትና ምርታማትን ለማሳደግ ይጥራል፡፡ • የፋብሪካን ምርት በዓይነትና በመጠን ለማደግ የሚረዱ የሰው ኃይል ፤የጥሬ ዕቃ የስራ ጊዜና የማሽን አሰራር ስልቶችን ያጠናል ስራ ላይም ያውላል፡፡ • የማምረቻ መሳሪያዎችና ሰራተኞች በስራ ላይ ጉዳት እንዳይደርስባቸው በቂ የአደጋ መከላከያ ዝግጅት እንዲኖር ያደርጋል፡፡ በአስፈላጊ ጊዜ እንዲሰራባቸው ያደርጋል፡፡ሰራተኞችም ለስራ የተሰጣቸውን ልብስና የአደጋ መከላከያ በአግባቡ መጠቀማቸውን ይቆጣጠራል፡፡ የእሳት አደጋ ብርጉድና የፖሊስ በድራሻዎች በጥበቃና በፈረቃ መሪዎች ተይዘው የእርዳታ ጥ እንዲያደረጉባቸው ያደርጋል በሮችም ሁልጊዜ ክፍት እንዲሆኑ መመሪያ ይሰጣል ያረጋግጣል፡፡ • የማምረቻና መገልገያ መሳሪያዎች በአግባቡ መያዛቸውንና ተከታታይነት ያለው እንክብካቤና ምርምር የተደረገባቸው መሆኑን ያረጋግጣል፡፡ ለዚህም የጥገና (የቴክኒክ ክፍሉ ባለው የውስጥ መመሪያ መሰረት በአስፈላው ዝግጅትና ቅንጅት እየተሰራበት መሆኑን ይመረምራል ያረጋግጣል፡፡ • በማንኛውም ጊዜ መሳሪያዎች አቀማመጥ ፤ የስራ እንቅስቃሴ ቦታ ምቹነት ፤የኤሌክትሪክ ኬብሎች ፤የአየር መስመሮች አዘረጋግና አቀማመጥ ከሰው ንኪኪ ነጻ መሆናቸውን ያረጋግጣልበትክክል ያልተዘረጉ ካሉም ቴክኒካዊ ባለው ሁኔታ እንዲያዙ ያደርጋል፡፡ • የማረቻ መሳሪያዎች የየራሳቸው ማህደር ተከፍቶላቸውና ዝርዝር ታካዊ መረጃዎች ተሟልተውላቸው እንዲያልፉ ያደርጋል፡፡ • የማቀላቀያና የማቀዝቀዥያ ማሽኖች የኤሌትክ አውቶማቲክ ተግባሮች በተፈለገው የጊዜ ገደብ ውስጥ መስራታቸውን በጌጃቸው በቅርበት ይቆጣጠራል፡፡ • የተዘጋጁት ግብዓቶች ከስሩ ባት የጉልት ሰራተኞች አማካኝት ወደ ማምረቻ ክፍል እንዲቀርቡ ያደርጋል፡፡ በምርት ሂደት የተበላሹ ምርቶች ቢኖሩ በማሽን በመፍጨትና እንደገና በመቀመም በግብዓትነት እንዲቀርቡ ያደርጋል፡፡ • የጥሬ ዕቃ ግብዓቶች ከስቶር በሰነድ በመረከብ በየቀኑ ለምጥጥን የተጠቀሙባቸውን በአይነትና በብዛት በቋሚ መዝገብ ያሰፍራ፡፡ የየሳምንቱንና ፤ የየወሩን የጥሬ ዕቃዎች ፍጆታን ሪፖርት ያቀርባል፡፡ • በአሰራር ወቅት የጥሬ ዕቃዎች ፍተሻ እንጥብጣቢና የሆነ አይነት ብክት እንዳይኖር በጥንቃቄ ይሰራል፡፡ • የጥሬ ዕቃዎች ከተፈቀደላቸው የሙቀትና የቅዝቃዜ መጠን ወይም የአየር ፀባይ ውጭ ለእርጥበትና ለመሳሰሉት ነገሮች እንዳይጋለጡ በጥንቃቄ ይይዛል፡፡ • በስራ ወቅት የሚፈጠሩትን ብናኞች በአካባቢው እየበነኑና እየተጠራቀሙ በሰራተኞችና በማሽኖች ላይ አደጋ እንዳያደርሱ በክፍሉ በቂ የአየር መተላለፊያ ክፍተት መኖሩን ያረጋግጣል፡፡ማሽኖችንና የኤሌትሪክ በርዶችን በየጊዜው እንዲጸዱ ያደርጋል፡፡ • ለእሳት አደጋ ማጥፊያ የተቀመጡት ኬሚካሎች አጠቃቀምንና አያያዝ በትክክል አውቆ ይጠብቃል፡፡ ስራ ላይም ያውላል ከስሩ ያሉት ሰራተኞች የስራ ልብሳቸውንና የአደጋ መከላከያዎቻቸውን በአግባቡ እንዲጠቀሙ ያደርጋል፡፡ ይቆጣጠራል፡፡ • ከስሩ የሚገኙትን ሰራተኞች የስራ ሰዓት አክባሪነትና የስራ አፈፃፀም ትጋት ይቆጣጠራል፡፡ የዲሲፕሊን ግድፈት ቢፈፅሙም ፈጥኖ ለቅርብ ኃላፊው ያሳውቃል፡፡ • የማቀላቀል ስራውን ሲያጠናቅቅ ፋብሪካ ውስጥ ገብቶ ተመሳሳይ ስራዎችን ያከናውናል፡፡ • የማቀላቀያና የማቀዝቀዣ መሳሪያዎቹ የተነሱበትንና የቆሙበትን እንዲሁም በማናቸውም አይት እክል ሲቆሙ ሰዓቶችን በትክክል ይመዘግባል፡፡ • በቅርብ ኃላፊው የሚሰጡትን ሌሎች ተመሳሳይ ስራዎችን ያከናውናል፡፡ ተገላጊ ችሎታ 10ኛ ክፍልና ከዚያ በላይ ያጠናቀቀና በቦታው በቂ የስራ ልምድ ያለው፡ የሰራተኛ ዝርዝር የስራ ድርሻና መመሪያ የስራ መደቡ መጠሪያ ፡- የጥገና ኃላፊ የስራ መደ,ቡ ተጠሪነት ፡-ለምርትና ቴክኒክ ስራ አስኪያጅ የስራ ቦታ፡- ቃሊቲ ሀ. ዋና ዋና ተግባሮች • የፕላስቲክ ማምረቻ አጠቃላይ የጥገና ስራዎችን በኃላፊነት ያስተባብራል፡፡ ይመራል • አጠቃላይ የፍተሻና የመከላከል እንዲሁም መደበኛ ያልሆኑና ያልተጠበቁ ብልሽቶችን የጥገና ስራዎችን ዕቅድና ፕግራም ያወጣል ሲፀድቅም በስራ ላይ ያውላል፡፡ • የማምረቻው የጥገና ክንዋኔ በበቂ ሪከርድ እየተያዘ በየወሩ መጨረሻ በሪፖርት እንዲቀርብ ያደርጋል፡፡ • የድርጅቱ ደንበኞችና መመሪያዎች በክፍሉ ያከብራል፡፡ ያስከብራል፡፡ ለ. ዝርዝር ተግባሮች • የፋብሪካው የዕለት ተዕለት አስፈላጊ ጥገና በስሩ ለሚገኙ ባለሙያ ሰራተኞች እንደ ክህሎታቸውና እንደየ ደረጃቸው እያየ ስራዎችን አአከፋፍሎ ያሰራል፡፡ • ለማምረቻ መሳሪያዎችና ድጋፍ ሰጪ አካሎቻቸው የተዘጋጁትን ወቅታዊ የፍተሻ የመከላከልና የብልሽት ጥገና ፕሮግራሞች ተግባራዊ እዲሆኑ ያደርጋል፡፡ • የየዕለቱ ሰራዎች ክንዋኔን በሚመለከት የተጀመሩበት ፤ የተጠናቀቁበትን ሰዓትና የፈጀወን መለዋወጫ የሰው ሀይልና የመሳሰሉት ወሳኝ ዳታዎችን በቋሚነት መዝገብ እንዲሰፍሩ ያደርጋል፡፡ • ለእያንዳንዱ ማምረቻ የሚያስፈልጉትን የኬሚካል ፤ ኤሌትሪካል ፤ ኒውማቲካል እና ሀይድሮሊካን መለዋወጫዎችን በዓይነትና በብዛት ለይቶ በማመልከት አስፈላጊና ወቅታዊ መጠባበቂያዎች በስቶር እንዲያዙ የግዢ ጥያቄ ያቀርባል፡፡ አቅርቦታውንም ይከታተላል፡፡ • በክፍሉ በሚከናወኑት ቴክኒካዊ የስራ ፀባዮች መሰረት ሰራተኞች የስራ ልብሶችንና የአደጋ መከላከያ መሳሪያዎች ተጠቅመው እንዲሰሩ ግንዛቤ ያስጨብጣል፡፡አስፈላጊውን ሁሉ እንዲሟሉ ያደርጋል አጠቃቀማቸውንም ይቆጣጠራል፡፡ • በሰሩ የሚገኙት ሰራተኞች የስራ ሰዓት ዲሲፕሊን ይቆጣጠራል፡፡ በየ6ወሩም የስራ አፈፃፀም ሪፖርት እየሞላ ያቀርባል፡፡ • ለሁሉም ማምረቻ መሳሪያዎች አስፈላጊ የሆኑ ማራራሻዎችን በሚመለከት (ዘይቶችና ግሪሶችን) በዓይነትና መጠን በመለየትና የአጠቃቀም ፕሮግራም በማውጣት ስራ ላይ እንዲውል ያደርጋል፡፡ ለዚሁም እንደአስፈላጊነቱ ቋሚ ግሪስ ማን አሰልጥኖ ይመድባል፡፡ • በማምረቻ መሳሪያዎች የኤሌትሪክ ሀይል ማከፋፈያዎችና መስመሮች ሁሉ የአደጋ ማሳወቂያና መከላከያ ምልክቶች እንዲኖሩ ያደርጋልል፡ • ለፋብሪካው አገልግሎት የተዘጋጁ ልዩ ልዩ የእሳት ማጥፊያ ኬሚካሎች የፎም ፤የሲኦቱና የውሃ መሳሪያ በተገቢው ቦታ እንዲያዙ በማድረግ በየጊዜው ፍተሻ ያደርጋል፡፡ ጊዜያቸው ሲደርስም እንደገና እንዲሞሉ ያደርጋል፡፡ ትክክለኛ ያስወግዳል፡፡ ይጠብቃል፡፡ • በተጨማሪም በቅርብ ኃላፊው የሚሰጡትን ተመሳሳይ ተግባራት ያከናውናል፡፡ ተፈላጊ የትምህርት ደረጃና የስራ ልምድ ከሙያና ቴክኒክ ትምህርት ተቋም በዲፕሎማ የተመረቀና የ4 ዓመት የስራ ልምድ ወይም ከተመሳሳይ የሙያ ተቋም በ10+3 የተመረቀና የ5 ዓመት የስራ ልምድ ያለው፡፡ የሰራተኛው ዝርዝር የስራ ድርሻና መመሪያ የስራ መደቡ መጠሪያ ፡- መካኒክ የቅርብ ኃላፊው ፡- ሲኒየር መካኒክ የስራ ቦታ ፡- ቃሊቲ ዋና ዋና ተግባራት ከቅርብ ኃላፊው በሚሰጠው የስራ ፕሮግራም መሰረት የማምረቻና የአገልግሎት መስጫ መሳሪያዎችን መፈተሸ ፤መካኒካል ጥገና ማድረግ፤ የፍተሻና የጥገና ስራ ውጤቶች እንዲመዘገቡ መረጃዎችን ማቅረብ፡፡ ለ. ዝርዝር ተግባራት • ከቅርብ አላፊው በሚደርሰው የእየለቱ የስራ ትዕዛዝ መሰረት ለማምረቻ አገልግሎት መስጫ መሳሪያዎች መካከለኛ የሆኑ ስራዎችን ያከናውናል፡፡ ስለ ክንውኑም ሪፖርት ያደርጋል፡፡፡ • የማረቻ መሳሪያዎች መካከል ብልሽት ይፈትሻል ፤መሳሪያዎች ለጥገና ከመቆማቸው በፊት አስፈላጊውን ክትትልና ምርመራ ያደርጋል፡፡ የብልሽት ምልክት ካለ ፈጥኖ በማሳወቅ የመከላከልና የጥገና እርምጃ ይወስዳል፡፡ • ለጥገና ስራ የዋሉትን ዕቃዎች የመሳሪያና የጥገና ስራው የተወሰደውን የማሽን የሰው ሰዓት መረጃ ይይዛል፡ ያስመዘግብል፡፡ • ለጥገና ስራ ውጭ የሚደረጉትን ዕቃዎች በአግባቡ ስራ ላይ ያውላል፡፡ ያገለገሉትም ሊጠገኑ እስከቻ ድረስ ታድሰው ለአገልግሎት እንዲዘጋጁ ያደርጋል፡፡ • የጥገናቸውን መሳሪያዎች ፈትሾ እና በትክክል መሰራታቸውን አረጋግጦ ለቅርብ ኃላፊው ያሳውቃል፡፡ • በማናቸውም አሰራር ቅድሚያ ለደህንነት ጥንቃቄ ሰጥቶና ለስራ የተሰጠውን ልብስም ሆነ የአደጋ መከላከያዎች በትክክል ይጠቀማል፡፡ • ከአቅሙ በላይ የሆነ የጥገና ስራ ለሲኒየር መካኒክ ወይም ለጥገና ኃላፊው ያሳውቃል፡፡ • ከቅርብ ኃላፊው ሲታዘዝ ሌሎች ተመሳሳይ ተግባራትን ያከናውናል፡፡ ተፈላጊ የትምህርት ደረጃና የስራ ልምድ ከሙያና ቴክኒክ ትምህት ቤት በጄኔራል መካኒክት ዲፕሎማና የ2 ዓመት የስራ ልምድ ያለው፡፡ የሰራተኛ ዝርዝር የስራ ድርሻና መመሪያ የስራ መደቡ መጠሪያ፡- ሲኒየር ጀነራል መካኒክ የቅርብ ኃላፊው ፡- ለጥገና ኃላፊ የስራ ቦታ ፡-ቃሊቲ ዋና ዋና ተግባራት ከተለያዩ የስራ ዘርፎች የሚደርሱ የጥገና ጥያቄዎችን መዝግቦ መረከብ ለሚመለከታቸው ባለሙያዎች ማከፋፈልና ማሰራት ፤የክፍሉ የጥገና መረጃዎችን መዝግቦ መያዝ ከስሩ የተመደቡትን ሰራተኞች ተቆጣጥሮ ማሰራት፡፡ ዝርዝር ተግባራት • በስራ ክፍሉ ሚዘጋጀውን የመካኒካልና የኒውማቲክ ጥገና ስራዎችን ለሚመለከታቸው ሰራተኖች በማከፋፈል ያሰራል፡፡ • ለጥገና የሚያስፈልጉ መፍቻዎችና ሌሎች የእጅ መሳሪያዎች ተሟልተው ለስራ ዝግጁ መሆናቸውን ያረጋግጣል፡፡ • ከተለያዩ የስራ ክፍሎች የሚቀርቡ የጥገና ጥያቄዎችን በጥንቃቄና በፍጥነት ተቀብሎ ይመዘግባል፡፡ ጥገናውን ያከናውናል፡፡ • ከመካኒኮችና ከጁንየር መካኒኮች አቅም በላይ የሆኑ ከባና ረቀቅ ያሉ ስራዎችን በራሱ ያከናውናል፡፡ • ለጥገና ስራ የሚያፈልጉ መለዋወጫ ዕቃዎችን ከመጋዘን ለማውጣት መጠየቂያ ሞልቶ ያቀርባል ፤ሲፈቀድም ተረክቦ ስራ ላይ ያውላል፡፡ • በጥገና ክፍሉ የተከናወኑ የአነስተኛ፤ መካከለኛና ከፍተኛ የጥገና መረጃዎችን እየመዘገበ ለቅርብ ኃላፊው ያቀርባል፡፡ • የማምረቻ የጥገና ክንዋኔዎችን በመደበኛ የመሳሪያው የህይወት ታሪክ ካርድ እንዲመዘገብ ያደርጋል፡፡ • በየዕለቱ የሰራቸው የእጅ መሳሪያዎች ወደ ስቶር መመለሳቸውን ያረጋግጣል፡፡ የጠፋ ካሉም የዕቃውን አይነትና መጠን በግልፅ ሪፖርት ያደርጋል፡፡ • የጥገና ወጭ የሚገልፅ መረጃ መዝገብ ይይዛል፡፡በስሩ ያሉት ሰራተኞች ተገቢውን መከላከያ ተጠቅመው መስራታቸውን ይቆጣጠራል፡፡በሰራተኞች የስራ አፈጻጸም ግምገማ ይሳተፋል፡፡ • በስራ አካባቢ አደጋ የሚያስነሱ ነገሮች በቂ የእሳት አደጋ መከላከያ የእያንዳንዱ ማሽን አካላት (ቺንጋዎች ፤ኮፕሊንጎች ፤ጥርሶች ወዘተ በአስተማማኝ ኮፈን /ሽፋን በማድረግ ከሰው ንክኪ ነጻ ያደርጋል፡፡ • ከስራ ሰዓት ውጪ ማሽኖች ፤ የኤሌትሪክ ቦርዶችና ብሬከሮች መቆማቸውን ያረጋግጣል፡፡ • ሰራተኞች በኮምፕሬሰር አየር ገላቸውን እንዳያፀዱ ይከለክላል፡፡ • የውና ፤የኤሌክትሪክ ፤የኮምፕሬሰር አየር ፤የሀይድሮሊክ ብክነቶችን ያስወግዳል፡፡ ይጠብቃል፡፡ • በተጨማሪም በቅርብ ኃላፊው የሚሰጡትን ተመሳሳይ ተግባራት ያከናውናል፡፡ ተፈላጊ የትምህርት ደረጃና የስራ ልምድ ከሙያና ቴክኒክ ትምህርት ተቋም በዲፕሎማ የተመረቀና የ4 ዓመት የስራ ልምድ ወይም ከተመሳሳይ የሙያ ተቋም በ10+3 የተመረቀና የ5 ዓመት የስራ ልምድ ያለው፡፡ የሰራተኛው ዝርዝር የስራ ድርሻና መመሪያ የስራ መደቡ መጠሪያ ፡- መካኒክ የቅርብ ኃላፊው ፡- ሲኒየር መካኒክ የስራ ቦታ ፡- ቃሊቲ ዋና ዋና ተግባራት ከቅርብ ኃላፊው በሚሰጠው የስራ ፕሮግራም መሰረት የማምረቻና የአገልግሎት መስጫ መሳሪያዎችን መፈተሸ ፤መካኒካል ጥገና ማድረግ፤ የፍተሻና የጥገና ስራ ውጤቶች እንዲመዘገቡ መረጃዎችን ማቅረብ፡፡ ዝርዝር ተግባራት • ከቅርብ አላፊው በሚደርሰው የእየለቱ የስራ ትዕዛዝ መሰረት ለማምረቻ አገልግሎት መስጫ መሳሪያዎች መካከለኛ የሆኑ ስራዎችን ያከናውናል፡፡ ስለ ክንውኑም ሪፖርት ያደርጋል፡፡፡ • የማምረቻ መሳሪያዎች መካከል ብልሽት ይፈትሻል ፤መሳሪያዎች ለጥገና ከመቆማቸው በፊት አስፈላጊውን ክትትልና ምርመራ ያደርጋል፡፡ የብልሽት ምልክት ካለ ፈጥኖ በማሳወቅ የመከላከልና የጥገና እርምጃ ይወስዳል፡፡ • ጥገና ስራ የዋሉትን ዕቃዎች የመሳሪያና የጥገና ስራው የተወሰደውን የማሽን የሰው ሰዓት መረጃ ይይዛል፡ ያስመዘግባል፡፡ • ለጥገና ስራ ውጭ የሚደረጉትን ዕቃዎች በአግባቡ ስራ ላይ ያውላል፡፡ ያገለገሉትም ሊጠገኑ እስከቻ ድረስ ታድሰው ለአገልግሎት እንዲዘጋጁ ያደርጋል፡፡ • የጥገናቸውን መሳሪያዎች ፈትሾ እና በትክክል መሰራታቸውን አረጋግጦ ለቅርብ ኃላፊው ያሳውቃል፡፡ • በማናቸውም አሰራር ቅድሚያ ለደህንነት ጥንቃቄ ሰጥቶና ለስራ የተሰጠውን ልብስም ሆነ የአደጋ መከላከያዎች በትክክል ይጠቀማል፡፡ • ከአቅሙ በላይ የሆነ የጥገና ስራ ለሲኒየር መካኒክ ወይም ለጥገና ኃላፊው ያሳውቃል፡፡ • ከቅርብ ኃላፊው ሲታዘዝ ሌሎች ተመሳሳይ ተግባራትን ያከናውናል፡፡ ተፈላጊ የትምህርት ደረጃና የስራ ልምድ ከሙያና ቴክኒክ ትምህት ቤት በጄኔራል መካኒክት ዲፕሎማና የ2 ዓመት የስራ ልምድ ያለው፡፡ የሰራተኛ ዝርዝር የሰራ ድርሻና መመሪያ የስራ መደቡ መጠሪያ፡- ሲኒየር ኤሌትሪሽያን የቅርብ ኃላፊው ፡- ለቴክኒክ /ለጥገና ኃላፊ የስራ ቦታ፡- ቃሊቲ ዋና ዋና ተግባራት ከቅርብ ኃላፊው በሚሰጠው መመሪያና የስራ ትዕዛዝ መሰረት ለማምረቻና መገልገያ መሳሪያዎች የሚውሉ ዕቃዎችና ማንኛውንም ኤሌክትሪክ ነክ ስራዎች በትክክል ስራ ላይ መዋላቸውን መከታተልና መቆጣጠር ፤ብልሽት ሲያጋጥምም መፈተሸና ጥገና ማድረግ፤ የኤሌክትሪክ መለዋወጫ ዕቃዎችንና መገልገያዎችን በበቂ ክምችት እንዲያዙ በማድረግ በጥንቃቄ ስራ ላይ ማዋል፡፡ ዝርዝር ተግባራት • የኤሌትሪካል የስራ እንቅስቃሴ በየዕለቱ እየተከታተለ ተገቢ ፍተሻዎችና የመከላከል ጥገናዎችን ያከናውና፡፡ (preventive maintenance) • የኤሌክትሪክ ሞተር መስመሮች ፤መሳሪያዎችና ማከፋፈያ ቦርዶች ዓይነት፤ ብዛት፤ደረጃና ፤የጭነት መጠን፤ የመለዋወጫ እቃዎችና ሌሎች የኤሌክትሪክ መረጃዎችና ስፕስፊኬሽኖችን መዝግ ይይዛል፡፡ • ኤሌክትሪካል ዲያግራሞችንና ማኑዋሎችን በአግባቡ ይዞ ይጠብቃል፤ይሰራባቸዋል፡፡ • የማምረቻና የመገልገያ መሳሪያዎች የስራ እንቅስቃሴ ባህርይን በማጥናት በሰውና በንብረት ላይ አደጋ ሊያደርሱ የሚችሉ ነገሮችን መከላከልና የአደጋ ማጥፊያ መሳሪየያዎችን እንዲሟሉ ያደርጋል፡፡ የኤሌክትሪክ መስመሮችና የኃይል ማከፋፈያ ቦርዶች ባሉባቸው ቦታዎች ሁሉ "አደጋ" በሚል ፅሁፍና አለማቀፋዊ መልዕክት ባላቸው የአደጋ ማሳወቂያ ምስሎች በማስቀመጥ ያስጠነቅቃል፡፡ • ከተለያዩ ክፍሎች የሚቀርቡ ኤሌክትሪካል የጥገና ጥያቄ ማቅረቢያ ቅፆችን ተቀብሎ በአግባቡ እንዲሞሉና እንዲከናወኑ በማድረግ በቋሚ ሪከርድ በትክክል እንዲመዘገቡ ያደርጋል፡፡ • ለኤሌክትሪክ ጥገና የሚያስፈልጉ የመለዋወጫ ዕቃዎችን በአይነት በብዛት ዝርዝርና የወጪ ዕቅድ ያዘጋጃል፤ ለኃላፊው በማቅረብ ያስወስናል፡፡ • ለኤሌክትሪካል ጥገና ስፍራ አስፈላጊ የሆኑ የመለዋወጫዎችና ሌሎች ዕቃዎች ግዢ ጥያቄ ያቀርባል፤ ሲፈቀድም ግዢውን ይከታተላል፡፡ • ለኤልክትሪካል ጥገና አስፈላጊ የሆኑ መለዋወጫዎችና አላቂ ዕቃዎች በበቂ መጠን በመጋዘን መኖራቸውን በየጊዜው ይከታተላል ለስራ የሚያስፈልጉትን መለዋወጫዎችን ከግምጃ ቤት በሰነድ ፈርሞ ይረከባል፤ ስራ ላይ ያውላል፤ የተቀሩትም በአግባቡ በመተማመኛ ተመላሽ ያደርጋል፡፡ • በስሩ ያሉትን ሰራተኞች ስራ ላይ አሰማርቶ ይቆጣጠራል፤ ከነሱ አቅም በላይ የሆነ የኤሌክትሪክ ጥገና ካለም በራሱ ያከናውናል፡፡ • ለኤሌክትሪክ ጥገና ስራ የዋሉ መለዋወጫዎችና ሌሎች ዕቃዎች ዝርዝር መረጃና ለጥገና ስራ የዋለው ወጭ በጥገና ጊዜ የባከነ ጊዜን በትክክል እንዲመዘገብ ያደርጋል፡፡ • የኤሌክትክ ቦርዶች /ፒኔሎችና የማሽኖች ላይ ብሬከሮች ጽዳት በየቀኑ እንዲጠበቅና እንዲፈተሸ ያደርጋል፡፡ የላሉ የሀይል ማስተላለፊያ ክሮችን ያጠብቃል፡፡ ሙሉ ሽፋን እንዲኖራቸው በማድረግ ከብናኝና ከመሳሰሉት እንዲጠበቁ ያደርጋል፡፡ • ጥገና የተደረገላቸው የማምረቻ መሳሪያዎች ስራ ከመጀመራቸው በፊት አስፈላጊውን ሙከራ አድርጎ በማረጋገጥ ስራ ላይ እንዲውሉ ለቅርብ ኃላፊው በማሳወቂያ ቅጽ ሪፖርት ያደርጋል፡፡ • ከስራ ሰዓት ውጪ የኤሌክትሪክ በሮች ፤ብሬከሮች እንዲቋረጡ ያደርጋል፤ ይቆልፋል ለስራ አስፈላጊ በሆነበት ሰዓት ቀድሞ ይከፍታል፡፡ በቂ አየር ማግኘታቸውንም ያረጋግጣል፡፡ • አስፈላጊ የሆኑ አዳዲስ የኤሌክትክ ዝርጋታዎች (installation work) በሚኖርበት ጊዜ ተገቢውን ፕላን እና ፕሮግራም እያዘጋጀ ይሰራል፡፡ • በተጨማሪም ሌሎች ተመሳሳይ ተግባራትን ሲታዘዝ ያከናውናል፡፡ ተፈላጊ የትምህርት ደረጃና የስራ ልምድ ከሙያና የቴክኒክ ትምህርት ቤት የኤሌክትሪሲቲ ዲፕሎማና የ4 ዓመት ልምድ፡፡ የጉልበት ሰራተኛ ተጠሪነቲ ፡- ለማሽን ኦፕሬተር የስራ ቦታ፡- ቃሊቲ ዝርዝር ተግባራት • የድርጅቱ የስራ ደንብ ፤ መመሪያና የስራ ሰዓትን ያከብራል፡፡ • በቅርብ ኃላፊው በየዕለቱ የሚሰጡትን ዕቃዎችን ማቅርብ ፤ የመደርደር ፤ የመቁረጥ የመሳሰሉትን ያከናውናል፡፡ • የማምረቻ መሳሪያዎችን በየእለቱ በተገቢው መንገድ ያጸዳል፡፡ • በማሽኖች ኦፕሬሽንና የስራ አካባቢን በማምረት ሂደት ለኦፕሬተሮች ሁለገብ የጉልበት እገዛ ይሰጣል፡፡ • የግብዓት አጉራሽ ቋቶችና ኮንበየሮች በግብዓት ቅመማና ማቀላቀያ ማሽኖች የሚከናወኑ ተግባሮችን አስፈላጊ በሆነበት ሰዓት በሁለገብነት ተግቶ ይሰራል፡፡ • የራሱን ችሎታ በየጊዜው ወደ ተሻለ ክህሎት ለማሳደግ በማሽኖች አሰራር ፤በምርቶች ጥራት ቁጥጥር ፤በውሃ አጠቃቀም ፤በሙቀት ፤በፍጥነትና በግፊት መቆጣጠሪያ መሳሪያዎች ያለውን አሰራር ለማወቅና በኃፊነት እገዛ ዕውቀትን ለማወቅ የማያቋርጥ ጥረት ማድረግ፡፡ • ለስራው የተሰጡትን የስራ ልብሶች ፤በቦታው የሚገኙትና የእሳት ማጥፊያ ኬሚካሎችና የእጅ መሳሪያዎችን በጥንቃቄ ይዞ ለስራው አገልግሎት ብቻ ያውላል፡፡ • ያለቁ ምርቶችን ወደ ውጭ ይጭናል፤ ያወርዳል፡፡ • በቅርብ ኃላፊው የሚሰጡትን ሌሎች ተመሳሳይና ተጨማሪ ስራዎችን ያከናውናል፡፡

PURPOSE The purpose of this procedure is to define the methods for preparing, reviewing, approving, registering and distributing new / revised documents and control documents from external origin within WF. 2. SCOPE This procedure applies to all quality system documents generated within WF, and it includes documents of external origins. 3. PROCESS OWNER Management Representative Approved by:Signature:Date: 7/10/2020 Name: Amanuel TesfayeDesignation: General Manager  4. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.1 Definition For the purpose of this document in addition to the definitions given in ISO 9000:2015 the following definitions apply Document: series of instructions or requirements that provides guidance/directions for performing work which affect the quality of WF’s product. A document can be in the form of hard copy, soft copy, film, etc. Document and data control: continues maintenance of documents in a valid state in all departments and functions Data: a set of information in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation or processing 4.2 Abbreviation MR: Management representative GM: General Manager DC: Document Control FLW: Flow chart ISO: International Organization for Standardization Doc: Document WF: Waterfit General Trading OP: Operating Procedure OF: Operating Form 5. PROCEDURE 5.1 Process flowchart Input Process Output Responsibility 1, OF/WF/001 2, Request for doc. creation/change/adoption 3, Approved request 4, Master list of doc. (OF/WF/004) 5, Documents Template Forms Template 6, Draft document 7, Reviewed draft document, OF/WF/002 8, Approved document, Master list (OF/WF/004) 9, Controlled document, OF/WF/003 No Yes No No Yes 1, Request for doc. Creation / change / adoption 2, Approved request 3, Verified document 4, Assigned document number 5, Draft document 6, Review notes 7, Approved document 8, Controlled document 9, Document receipt acknowledgement 1, Any WF’ employee 2, Manager / Heads in their area of responsibilities 3, MR 4, MR 5, Assigned document writer 6, Requester 7, Manages / Heads in their area of responsibilities / GM 8, MR 9, MR 5.2 Description of process steps FLW Process Steps Description 1 Document creation or change or adoption request may be raised from any WF’s employee using the form OF/WF/001 2 The request should be approved by the managers/heads in their area of responsibility. The request might be rejected. The main reasons for rejection of document creation request may be the following. When there is an existing document for the job in question. When there is no existing process/activity to be defined by the proposed document. When training is sufficient for the job in question. Document change or disposal request is rejected when the requester fails to provide adequate justification for the change. When requests are rejected the reasons for rejection shall be recorded and maintained and notified to the requester. 3 Document creation or change request shall be reviewed against master list of documents and risk of undertaking undocumented job. 4 The Management Representative shall assign document numbers and shall record the assigned number on Master List of Document Number. 5 A competent person shall be assigned to write new documents or make changes on documents. The document writer shall write the document considering the level of education of the employees who will be using the document and risks and criticality of the process to be defined by the document. Document language shall be determined in advance. The document writer shall organize the document in accordance with Documents and Form Templates 6 The requester should review the draft document. The review shall include: Clarity Completeness Complying with the documents and form templates Legibility 7 Additional description is not required 8 The Management Representative: Shall issue document number; Shall make required copies of document for issuing; Shall retain and file the original copy of documents; Using a rubber stump shall indicate on all document(except forms) , “Date of Issue”, “Copy Number” and “Registration Number”; Shall register documents on “Documents Master List. 9 The Management Representative shall issue documents to the locations where they are needed. In the case of documents change, the old (obsolete) documents shall be returned to The Management Representative, and The Management Representative shall dispose the documents. Recipient of the document shall acknowledge by signing on the Document Release Note and returning it to The Management Representative. 5.3 Additional description to the process steps 5.3.1 Document coding system 5.3.1.1 Sequence of document code for procedures The sequence of procedures and work instructions code runs as follow. 1st OP: Operating Procedures and WI for Work Instructions. 2nd WF: Waterfit General Trading 3rd Document Serial number with three digits EXAMPLE: MN/WF/001 EXAMPLE: OP/WF/001 EXAMPLE: WI /WF/ 001 EXAMPLE: OF / WF/ 001 EXAMPLE: EX / WF / 001 5.3.2 Contents of procedures The general formats for procedures are as follows. 5.3.2.1 Issue history List all issues of the procedure from initial release to current issue. Description of the change shall be a summary of change made. 5.3.2.2 Reference documents List reference documents by their control number and title (this does not include forms) 5.3.2.3 Contents Contents of the document with its page number shall be described. 5.3.2.4 Purpose Describe the main purpose of the procedure 5.3.2.5 Scope Describe the area or subject where the procedure is applicable. 5.3.2.6 Process owner Describe the overall owner of the process. 5.3.3.7 Definitions and abbreviations Clarify (if applicable) abbreviation and/or terms used in the procedure. 5.3.2.8 Procedure Describe the process steps clearly and adequately. 5.3.2.9 Records List the records that must be generated and maintained to demonstrate that the requirements of the procedure have been fulfilled. 5.3.2.10 Related Documents List all related documents applicable to the procedure. 5.3.3 General page layout 5.3.3.1 Format typographical specifications The following specifications are all typographical matter: 1) Fonts Font style – Times New Roman Font size Organization Name - 12-point, uppercase and bold. Document number - 12-point, uppercase and normal. Issue number- 12-point, uppercase and normal. Page number - 12-point and normal. Approved By, Date: 10-point and bold Footer note: 10-point, normal, and uppercase Document title, 14-point, Title case and bold. Main Headings - 12-point, uppercase and bold. Sub-headings - 12-point, Sentence case and bold. Body Text – Default font size 12 points; but as appropriate it can be not less than 7 points and more, Justified and normal or bold. 2) General format for developing forms All forms generated in Waterfit General Trading shall conform to the format as shown in Annex B. 5.3.3.2 Control of external documents The Management Representative shall receive from archive and register all external documents. MR shall make the required copies of the external documents and issue to the locations where they needed for implementation after identifying the document with rubber stamp labeled with “Document Number”, “Copy Number”, “Date of Issue” and “Signature”. 5.3.3.3 All document control systems shall address the following requirements New documents and changes to existing documents shall be reviewed and approved for adequacy and completeness by the responsible person before release for implementation. All documents shall be legible, dated, readily identifiable with unique numbers, titles, and revision levels, and maintained in an orderly manner. Documents shall be readily available to all users within WF. External documents shall be properly identified and distributed for users and removed from all location when they become obsolete. A separate master list shall also be prepared and maintained by the Management Representative. The latest approved policies, regulations and directives shall be properly identified and available to users. Forms associated with QMS documentation shall be controlled. Each form shall be uniquely identified indicating the latest approved version. Work Languages Shall be Amharic and English. 5.3.3.4 Documents Control Stamp Templates For Controlled Documents (Blue Stamp) CONTROLLED QMS DOCUMENTS COPY NUMBER DATE OF ISSUE (DD/MM/YY) SIGNATURE, MR For External Documents (Blue Stamp) EXTERNAL DOCUMENTS DOCUMENT NUMBER COPY NUMBER DATE OF ISSUE (DD/MM/YY) SIGNATURE, MR For Obsolete Documents (Red Stamp) OBSOLETE DOCUMENTS DATE (DD/MM/YY) SIGNATURE, MR 6. RISKS Error when registering the document preparation, change & adoption request Reviewing & Approvals take too long Master list not updated Typing error Misunderstanding the draft document Computer/software breakdown Releasing wrong document 7. Records in a filing system shall be categorized as follow: a) First level category - identifies the functions Categorize the records based on the specific Department/Service/Branch Office and these are designated by two uppercase English Alphabets as Follows. b) Second level category - Identifies the record Two digit numerical codes starting from 01 to 99 shall be assigned to each process/activity identified in each Second level category. c) File serial number - Identifies the specific file (volume) Every file shall be allocated a file number clearly identifying the year of creation (Gregorian or Ethiopian Calendar). d) File Coding System 5.3.2 Closing Files When a process/an activity associated to the file are terminated, the file shall be closed using Form No. OF/WF/009. PURPOSE The purpose of this procedure is to define the method to undertake Quality Management System audit in all aspects of the quality system described within the Quality Manual and associated procedures and instructions to ensure compliance to all documented system requirements, initiate corrective actions and verify its clearness by follow-up audit. 2. SCOPE This procedure applies to all quality system audits undertaken within WF. 3. PROCESS OWNER Management Representative Approved by:Signature:Date: Name: Amanuel TesfayeDesignation: General Manager  4. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.1 Definitions For the purpose of this document in addition to the definitions given in ISO 9000:2015 the following definitions shall be used. Quality audit: A systematic and independent examination to determine whether quality activities and related results comply with planned arrangements and whether these arrangements are implemented effectively and are suitable to achieve objectives. Auditor: A person with the competence to conduct an audit. Auditee: Function being audited. 4.2 Abbreviations WF: Waterfit General Trading GM: General Manager MR: Management Representative FLW: Flow Chart OP: Operating Procedure OF: Operating Form CAR: Corrective Action Report NCR: Non Conformity Report 5. PROCEDURE 5.1 Flowchart INPUT PROCESS OUTPUT RESPONSIBILITY 1. Annual audit program 2. Auditor& Audit team leader 11. Auditor 12. Audit team leader 13. Audit team leader, MR 5.2 Description of process steps FLW Process Steps 1 The Management Representative shall initiate the quality audit by assigning the audit team leader and fix mutually convenient time schedule. The team leader shall be qualified auditor. 2 The Management Representative and the Audit Team Leader shall define the audit objectives, scope & criteria. The audit objectives define what is to be accomplished by the audit and the audit scope describes the extent and boundaries of the audit. 3 The audit team members shall be selected taking in to account the competence needed to achieve the objectives of the audit and hence comprise personnel qualified as auditors. The Audit team leader shall decide the size and composition of the team. 4 The Audit Team Leader & Management Representative shall formally contact the auditee to make arrangement for the audit and to provide in formation on the proposed timing and the team composition. 5 The auditee documentation such as management system documents records and previous audit reports shall be reviewed to determine its conformity with audit criteria, before conducting the actual audit. 6 Description is not required for this process step 6.1 The internal quality audit process shall be terminated if the system as documented does not conform to the audit criteria. 7 The auditor shall prepare the audit plan to facilitate scheduling and coordination of the audit activities. The audit plan shall include the following:- The audit objectives and scope; The audit criteria and any reference documents; The date and places where the audit is to be conducted ; The expected time and duration of the audit, including meetings with the auditee management and audit team meetings; The roles and responsibilities of the audit team members and accompanying persons; Identification of the auditee's representative for the audit; Matters related to confidentiality and Audit report topics, distribution and expected date of issue The audit team members shall prepare and organize working documents according to their audit assignments. The working documents may include:- Checklists and audit sampling plans and Forms for recording information. 8 The audit plan shall be reviewed and approved by the Audit team leader and shall be accepted by the auditee management. Auditors shall sign confidentially statement and this will be sent to the auditee along with the audit plan. 9 The approved audit plan shall be distributed to the auditee at least a week before the audit activities begin. 10 An opening meeting shall be held with the auditee's management or where appropriate those responsible for the functions or processes to be audited. The purpose of the opening meeting is: - to confirm the audit plan - to provide a short summary of how the audit activities will be undertaken - to confirm communication channels, and - to provide an opportunity for the auditee to ask questions From the audit team member's personnel independent of those having direct responsibility for the process/activity being audited shall conduct the audit. Information shall be collected through interviews, examination of documents and observation of activities and conditions in the area of concern and shall be verified. Information gathered through interview shall be tested by acquiring the same other independent sources, such as physical observation, measurement and records. Clues suggesting non-conformities shall be noted if they seem significant even though not covered by checklists. When non-conformities are identified it shall be agreed with the auditee. The auditee shall determine the causes of the identified and agreed non-conformities and their respective corrective action(s) If the auditee is not being able to identify and propose the solution, the duration to clear the non conformities shall be agreed. Closing meeting shall be held with the auditee for the following purposes: To present the final results, main findings and CARs. To receive confirmation from the Management Representative that they have understood and agreed. To reinforce the senior management's obligations. To give a positive feedback to those workers who contribute towards the quality system. Offering the opportunity to respond to the principal findings. The implementation and effectiveness of the corrective actions shall be undertaken by the auditee with in an agreed time frame. The auditee shall follow the status of the corrective action and inform the MR. Subsequently the Management Representative shall assign the auditor to under take follow-up audit The completion and effectiveness of corrective actions shall be verified by the follow up audit or be part of the subsequent audit. 11 The auditor shall prepare the audit report. The audit report shall include:- Objectives and scope of the audit Identification of audit team leader and members The dates and places where the audit activities were conducted The audit criteria The audit finding The audit conclusions Distribution list for the audit report. The audit plan Audit reports shall be clear, concise and legible and supported by objective evidence. 12 The audit team leader shall review and approve the audit report for completeness and clarity. 13 The approved audit report shall be distributed to recipients according to the distribution list and within the agreed time period. The audit team members, those responsible for managing the audit and all report recipients shall respect and maintain the confidentiality of the contents of documents, any other information obtained during the audit, and the audit report. All draft working documents pertaining to the audit shall be retained or destroyed by agreement between the participating parities 5.3 Supplements to the process steps 5.3.1 At least once per year, all elements of the Quality System must be audited against documented requirements to ensure compliance. These audits are scheduled by the Management Representative and, unless otherwise indicated. Random sampling of records, actual witnessed activities, current document files, and other related records and functions are to be reviewed against the documented requirements to verify compliance. All non-conformities shall be addressed in a timely manner and corrective actions shall be implemented to ensure compliance to ISO 9001:2015 standard, documented procedures, work instructions and Quality Manual. Results of all internal audit reports shall be submitted for the management review. Auditors shall possess personal attributes to enable them to act in accordance with the principles of auditing. Auditor should be open-minded and mature; possess sound judgments; analytical skill and tenacity; have the ability to perceive situations in a realistic way, to understand complex operations from a broad perspective, sincere, honest & discrete, diplomatic decisive, act and function independently while interacting effectively with others and to understand the role of individual units within the overall organization. Personal traits of an auditor shall include the following: Desirable Good outward impression - appearance and conduct; Intelligent - alert, understanding, well spoken and reasoning; Emotionally stable - clam, self-confident, persistent, insistent, task orientated, resilient; Good character - honest, reliable constructive, helpful and diplomatic, patient, sober, discreet; Good attitude - values, interest, work habits, initiative, careful, curious and open-minded, unbiased, attentive, observant. Undesirable Poor outward impression - undisciplined, opinionated and argumentative; Lacks intelligence - injudicious and gullible; Emotionally unstable - bad tempered, lazy, unsure, depressive; Bad character - dishonest, impatient, unreliable; Poor attitude - easily persuaded, inferiority complex, needs popularity. Questioning is employed in order to ensure that the facts presented are indeed correct and that they are a true reflection of the operations. The main tool an auditor may use during questioning is using open questions or closed questions according to the circumstances. When starting the audit, open questions should be employed in combination with good listening techniques. The auditor will use closed questions when he/she wishes to obtain concrete and focused facts. 6. RISKS Turnover of personnel who took the Audit training Absence of Auditor & Auditee Overlooking insignificant gaps Review & Approvals take too long Unfairly distributed times for the audit Audits take too long Audit report writing take too long 7. D0114: ISSUE HISTORY Issue Description of Change Originator Effective Date 1 Initial Release Task Force REFERENCE DOCUMENTS Document Number Document Title EX/WF/001 ISO 9001: 2015 Quality Management System – Requirements CONTENT Page 1 PURPOSE 1 2 SCOPE 1 3 PROCESS OWNER 1 4 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 2 5 PROCEDURE 3 6 RISKS 6 7 RECORDS 6 8 RELATED DOCUMENTS 6 FOR DOCUMENT CONTROL USE ONLY PURPOSE The purpose of this procedure is to define the methods for reviewing: (1) The working of the quality system i.e., whether procedures are being followed, whether the system is continuing to meet ISO 9001:2015 standard requirements, and whether the objectives of the quality system are being achieved; (2) the quality problems and proposed solutions; and (3) to define the methods to agree and authorize changes in the quality system. SCOPE This procedure is applicable during review of the Quality Management System implemented within WF. 3. PROCESS OWNER All Department Heads or Process Owners Approved by:Signature:Date: Name: Amanuel TesfayeDesignation: General Manager  4. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.1 Definitions For the purpose of this document in addition to the definitions given in ISO 9000:2015, the following definitions apply. Participating persons: Persons who contribute ideas (who have voice) in the management review meetings and these persons are the management committee members Observers: Persons who attend the meetings but do not participate to contribute ideas. 4.2 Abbreviations WF: Waterfit General Trading GM: General Manager MR: Management Representative FLW: Flowchart MCM: Management Committee Members MRM: Management Review Meeting OP: Operating Procedure OF: Operating Form 5. PROCEDURE 5.1 Process Flowchart INPUTS PROCESSES OUTPUTS RESPONSIBILITY 1. Annual Plan 2. List of Participants Agendas for the meeting OF/WF/017 OF/WF/019 Initiated and registered Draft Agendas Minutes Review Report, Signed Receipt, Acknowledgement Initiated Action(s) Implemented proposed actions MR GM (Chairperson) MR MR Respective Departments 5.2 Description of process steps FLW Process Description 1 Based on the annual management review schedule the Management Representative initiates the management review to be conducted. The initiated meeting shall be held when it is approved by the GM. 2 The management review meeting begins with confirmation of the minutes of the last review, if any. The management committee shall review the quality system, based on the organization policy, objectives, plans, criteria documents and procedures. The agenda for the review may be: the status of actions from previous management reviews; changes in external and internal issues that are relevant to the quality management system; information on the performance and effectiveness of the Quality Management System, including trends in: customer satisfaction and feedback from relevant interested parties; the extent to which quality objectives have been met; process performance and conformity of products and services; nonconformities and corrective actions; monitoring and measurement results; audit results; the performance of external providers; the adequacy of resources; the effectiveness of actions taken to address risks and opportunities (see 6.1); Opportunities for improvement. The outputs from the management review shall include any decisions and actions related to: opportunities for improvement; any need for changes to the quality management system, and Resource needs. 3 The Management Representative is responsible to register (each with unique identification code) and circulate the minutes of the management review to the MCM not later than 5 working days from the date of the review conducted. The Management Representative is responsible for the distribution of the minutes of the management review to the concerned persons other than the MCM. 4 The Management Representative, when necessary, based on the results of the management review shall initiate preventive and/or corrective action to be taken by the respective Directorates/Services. If actual and/or potential non-conformities are not identified, the management review process is finalized. 5 Department heads have the primary responsibility to ensure that proposed actions have been planned and implemented without undue delay and ensure their effectiveness. Implementation status report shall be submitted to the Management Representative as stipulated on the action plan. 5.3 Additional process description The management review meeting shall represent all the MCM of the Authority. Apart from the MCM, others may be invited regularly or occasionally. The review meeting shall be conducted in the presence of the GM or his representative. The MRM shall be held at least twice a year. The Management Representative is responsible to prepare the yearly schedule as well as to initiate more frequent review meetings, especially at the early stage of implementation of the quality system. The MRM shall be held in a formal way i.e., with a chairperson, meeting secretary and formal agenda. The MRM needs information on various aspects of the working of the quality system and the Management Representative shall present a formal report on what has happened since the last review meetings. The Minutes shall be distributed to MCM, in writing, in advance of the meeting and later this report shall be attached with the minutes of the management review. 6. RISKS Absence of meeting participants Another urgent meeting needed for other routine works Meeting halls occupied for another meeting Meeting take too long Off agenda discussions Disagreements when discussions and decisions Missed points when preparing the minute Confirmation of minute take too long Follow-up actions take too long 7. RECORDS The Management Representative shall keep: Management review program Minutes of the management review Corrective Actions Taken 8. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.1 Definitions Participating persons: Persons who contribute ideas (who have voice) in the meetings and these persons are the committee members. Observers: Persons who attend the meetings but they do not participate to contribute ideas. Quorum: A majority of its members. 4.2 Abbreviations WF: Waterfit General Trading OP: Operating Procedure OF: Operating Form FLW: Flowchart GM: General Manager 5 PROCEDURES 5.1 Process flowchart Input Process Output Responsibility 1.Plan & identified agendas 2.Agenda, participants & meeting notification form 3. Signed notification form 4. Initial records of the meeting & minutes writing form 5. Minutes 6. Confirmed Minutes 1. Initiated Meeting 2.Signed notification form 3.Initial Records of the Meeting 4. Minutes 5. Confirmed Minutes 6. Initiated Action 1. Chairperson 2. Secretary 3. Chairperson 4. Secretary 5. Secretary 6. Secretary 5.2 Description of Process Steps FLW Process steps 1 The chairperson initiates all other meetings. The initiation may be based on the annual plan or specific problem. Any function may raise a request to the Director as the case may be. 2 The secretary appointed by the chairperson or by any other authorized person shall clearly and briefly prepare the agenda in consolation with the chairperson. The agenda shall be circulated together with the accompanied documents/records. 3 The meeting shall be held only if the simple majority (50 %+) of the participants are present. The meeting begins with confirmation of the minutes of the last review, if any, and then approves the agenda for the day. Decisions are passed by the majority vote, provided, however, that the chairperson shall have a casting vote in case of a tie. Depending on the prevailing conditions the meeting shall be held either in Amharic or English languages. The meeting shall be cancelled if quorum is not reached or due to other urgent /priority matters and the reasons shall be recorded. 4 Minutes shall be prepared as soon as possible as notes tend to lose their meaning over time. The minutes shall be clear, concise and a true record of the meeting. A record of what each person said at the meeting is not necessary; however, if there is a major split in opinion on important issues, the different view shall be recorded. Minutes shall be written in the third person and the pas tense. Decisions shall be stated verbatim (exactly what the participants have said). Contents of minutes shall be as described on OF/WF/023. Minutes shall be numbered (uniquely identified). 5 The minutes shall be circulated to the participants without undue delay. The Chairperson is responsible to circulate the minutes to concerned persons/ functions other than the participants. The meeting participants shall review the minutes thoroughly and confirm its acceptance by signing on it. If meeting participants is not accepting a particular section of the minutes, he/she shall describe clearly the reasons for not accepting to the Secretary. If the Secretary agrees with the proposed change on the minutes he/ she make the change in consolation with the chairperson and re-circulate the minute for confirmation. If the Secretary is not convinced he/she notifies the chairperson immediately and the chairperson calls a meeting to decide on the proposed change on the minutes. 6 The chairperson when necessary based on the results of the meeting shall initiate action to be taken 6. RISKS Absence of meeting participants Meeting taking longer time than expected Off agenda discussions Disagreements when discussions and decisions Missed points when preparing the minute Confirmation of minute taking longer time than expected Follow-up actions taking longer time than expected 7. PROCESS OWNER Administration & Human Resource Department Approved by:Signature:Date: Name: Amanuel Tesfaye Designation: General Manager 4. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.1 Definition Human Resource The field of business concerned with recruiting and managing employees Abbreviations GM: General Manager FLW: Flowchart HRM: Human Resource Management A&HR: Administration & HR Department OP: Operating Procedure OF: Operating Form WF: Waterfit General Trading 5. PROCESS DESCRIPTION Terminations could be: Probationary Termination The Company can terminate the employment of an employee on probation before the expiry of the probationary period. The decision shall be based upon an objective assessment of the performance of the employee. A one-week prior notice shall be given in cases of probationary termination. Disciplinary Termination Disciplinary termination shall take place when an employee commits a major offense or repeated minor offenses. Summary dismissals shall take place without notice while other terminations shall require a prior notice of up to a maximum of two weeks. Waterfit has applied all the rule and regulation of Proclamation no.1156/2019 Labor Proclamation. Resignation All regular or contractual employees shall have the right to resign from their services giving in writing a one-month notice or for managers’ three months notice. The letter should be addressed to the immediate supervisor. The GM can waive or reduce the requirement of the notice period if it is of disadvantage to the company. GM / A&HR could negotiate with the employee for the advantage of the company. Absence from work without good cause or notice for over five consecutive working days shall be considered resignation without notice and the company shall retain the right to terminate the employment of the employee in accordance with the disciplinary provisions stipulated in this policy. The employee should fill an exit form. Completion of a Project or a Job The Company shall reserve the right to terminate the employment of regular or contractual employees upon completion of a project or a job and in the event high performing employees cannot be transferred elsewhere. Poor Performance The employment of any regular or contractual employee may be terminated due to inability to perform prescribed duties in a satisfactory manner. Before such termination takes place, the employee shall be informed of his/her deficiencies verbally as well as in writing. In the event not being able to improve performance on the part of the employee, a written proposal to terminate the employment shall be forwarded to the next level supervisor. The possibility of retaining an employee who could perform well in a lower grade shall be explored before a termination letter is issued. Such a decision shall be made by GM as per delegation upon the consent of the concerned individual. The decision to terminate the employment of an employee shall be made in writing by the General Manager as per delegation. Such termination shall take place with a one month prior notice. Imprisonment or Conviction of an Offense Absence from work due to a sentence of imprisonment passed against an employee for more than thirty days shall subject him/her to termination without notice. Moreover, an employee's employment shall be terminated if he/she is convicted for a crime where such conviction renders him/her unsuitable for the Company. Expiry of Contract of Employment The employment of a contractual employee shall be terminated without notice upon the expiry of the contract period. Such termination shall take place if there are no possibilities of redeployment for high performing employees. In the case of a possibility of redeployment, the employee will be notified one month earlier. Redundancy The service of a regular or contractual employee can be terminated with notice when the operation of the Company requires the cancellation of the post of the employee or reclassification of posts. The period of notice for such termination shall be a) one month in the case of an employee who has completed his/her probation and served less than one year, and b) two months for employees with more than one-year service. The notice of termination shall be made in writing and state the reasons for and effective date of the termination. Death Death of an employee shall automatically mean termination of employment. The last day of the Ethiopian month in which the death has occurred shall be taken as the date of termination for the purpose of termination benefits. Retirement The mandatory retirement age for employees at the company shall be 60 years. However, if an aged employee is found extremely suitable for the job, he/she shall be made to continue. The decision to extend the services of an employee who has reached the retirement age shall be made by the General Manager. A notice period of one month shall be given to a retiring employee in writing by Administration. WF has applied all the rule and regulation of proclamation no. 715/2003 private servant proclamation. Cessation of the Organization If an event which entails cessation of the Company in part or whole, temporarily or permanently occurs termination of the services of employees shall take place. In case of a partial cessation, the selection process shall be carried out by the GM & A&HR. The guidelines of the Labor Proclamation shall be used for selection. Health Problems The employment of a regular or contractual employee can be terminated if he/she is, for reasons of health or disability, unable to carry out his/her obligations under the terms of employment. The employment of an employee who absents herself /himself beyond the sick leave entitlement of six months in any twelve months' period shall be subject to termination due to health problems. Unwillingness to Accept Transfer Decisions The employment of a regular or contractual employee can be terminated if he/she is unwilling to accept decisions of change of duty station. Such an employee shall be issued a termination letter by the GM and the termination shall be effected with one month notice. When employee contract is terminated; employee shall have clearance signed by respective departments except the probationary period termination. A&HR shall communicate with other respective departments and maintain all records in this process. Process Step Description FLW Description • Identify of Fixed Asset Fixed Asset consists of all property owned by the company with a useful life of more than one year and a minimum cost of Br 1000 are categorized under this group. Items under 1000 Br are expensed automatically and registered by stores and by central procurement &Supply department. This type of fixed asset counts every annual inventory year from the last year inventory compare to the actual year inventory the shortage items report immediately. *Items in the store that has fixed asset nature and not issued from the store until issued date should not be included in this category; rather they will be included as stock items. • Fixed Asset Register Fixed Asset register is the format to use the WFfixed asset items separately recorded on registration book or fixed asset cards, this card or registration book contains description, identification number, serial number building size(for building),model, unit of measurement, date of purchase, supplier, date of manufacturer, cost, annual depreciation rate, estimated life, location & table calculate depreciation. The format used to recorded full information regarding the Fixed Asset and to compute depreciation this format to should be kept in the general inventories controller and shall be checked during the inventory year and to control the property condition. • Categories of fixed Assets We classify our fixed assets/ non-current assets above1000 Br in 9groups. The principal accounting Policies adopted by WF are stated below:- • FA is stated at cost less accumulated depreciation. • Depreciation is computed in accordance with proclamation No.979/2008 on straight line basis using the following per annum • FA acquired before Sene 30, 2008E.C would continue to depreciate on a reducing balance method except for buildings which had been depreciated on a straight line basis. • LEASE HOLD LAND:-It is stated atcost less amortization. Amortization is charged over a period of lease term. Recording All fixed Asset above 1000 Br should be identified and recorded in a Fixed Asset Register. They will be physically verified in regular intervals and at the time of acquisition each asset should be given an individual identification number. Identification Number (fixed Asset label) The identification number tag to the fixed asset to made for aluminum label or another material. The existence of identification number tags should be checked on the assets during the inventory and controlling time. If missed then it should be retagged. Please follow the figure on the label of fixed asset e.g. WF-01-001-001 WF: Number next to stands for notifying it is a fixed asset Number in the middle stands for group (asset type) The last numbers is for fixed assets serial number N.B: each fixed asset’s serial number has to indicate all the information about specific item. • Cost and depreciation The cost of the assets should be capitalized and presented to the company balance sheet. Then in each accounting period a depreciation charge is levied on the income and expenditure account to write off the cost of asset as the same time the contra asset account of the asset i.e. accumulated depreciation shown on the Balance Sheet. Thus we split the cost of these assets out over a number of years to reflect the contribution they make to the service we provide in future years. As an alternative to the actual cost competent valuation may be done as a basis for the initial cost for the first year depreciation is calculated from the assets purchased date to end of the year. Land No Depreciation For Building 20years 5% Computer & Printers 5years 20% Others 6.67 years 15% For fully depreciated fixed assets, their value should be recorded as birr 1.00 to show the asset depreciated fully. • Disposal Of Fixed Asset After annual inventory of fixed Asset, the fixed asset items condition properly records by the attached format of the condition of FA describes by very good, good, fair, non –function, damage, by use of this description, the count committee identifies the fixed assets whether non-functional or need maintenance. An inventory can be taken at any time using this process; however a full physical inventory must be taken in December 8& July7to have a reconciled inventory for the fiscal year and to provide data for the determination of cost of service, cost of annual ending inventory & inventory report. 2. SCOPE The scope of this procedure applies to all materials annual inventory in WFfrom the counting period up to the final report period. It takes approximately from 45-60 days from starting date usually December 8& July7of each year. 3. PROCESS OWNER PSD, FinanceDepartment Approved by: Signature: Date: 7/10/2020 Name: Amanuel Tesfaye Designation: General Manager 4. DEFINITIONS 4.1. Definition Physical inventory; isan actual count of items/merchandise & non-merchandise/ ininventory as contrasted with accepting the value shown on accounting record.
