Process Steps Description FLW Description 1. Notify the warehouse and all department All annual inventories must be scheduled. This annual inventory schedule informs all user departments by official letter before 3 week from starting date. All responsibility ofWFemployee to accomplish the annual inventory period effectively, it needs more coordination and time management. The goal of the annual inventory count is to obtained accurate information about inventories on hand which should be help to make right business decision, an alternative to a full physical inventory when all inventory is counted at a point in time is inventory cycle counts when you count inventory in portion throughout a year. Important reasons why a company conduct a physical inventory? • To verify or ascertain the physical count, condition and location of merchandise & non- merchandise inventory items and to ensure that it is properly documented. • To identify, document and add items to its inventory list that are on-hand and meet qualifying criteria but are not currently shown as part of inventory. • To ensure that legitimately transferred or disposed of items are no longer carried on the inventory listing and finally to identify any missing or damaged items that need to be located, repaired or replaced. • The most obvious reasons are that you conduct a physical inventory to check it the inventory accounting record are accurate and complete at a particular time. • Physical inventory is not only an accounting requirement but also accurate stock quantity of WFmore likely to be successful completion of constructed house and also have better control of company stock levels and company money. • Should be to order the goods in the right quantity at the proper time avoiding over or under stock. 2. Organization Of a committee member A committee composed of three- sevenmembers to be organized at head office and branches level also designated by General Manager/ Deputy General Manager then orientation needs to be given based on this procedure on how to undertake inventory. The committees’ member needs to have the ability and experience of undertaking inventory and reporting on their finding and observation. More than one committee can be organized for fixed assets, Non-fixed assets, stock items and vehicles inventory to minimize work load. A committee which designated for the head office and branches might be segregated its duties by types of assets or locations to minimize work load. 3 Planning & Preparation A physical inventory is a time and resource consuming procedure which requires proper planning. The planning helps the warehouse and the committee member to make annual physical inventory counts more effective. Establishment and documentation of counting procedure will allow to control and supervise physical inventory properly. First, should be determining a date and time of conducting a physical inventory and inform all departments about it. Physical inventory counting takes place on different days because of several remote warehouse select a day when the company activities low. Second, choose the methods of conducting a physical inventory in WFselect the best method, this method is A COUNT SHEET METHOD this method pre-printed lists of inventory (usually generated by company soft copy) are used to record on hand count. This method the easiest and cheapest method less time consuming, searching counting, comparing and recording. A lot of time spent to find particular items during wall to wall counts items which are not in the listing or not in their place could be missed. Third, should be prepare the warehouse make sure that all stock items are in their proper places and can be clearly identified clean up the store area, label all shelves and location, slow moving and nonmoving items can be counted and marked a day before a full physical inventory. Identify damage, discounted and absolute classes of items places them separately from inventory prepare and provide the plan of stock location. In the last make sure all inventory is clearly identified and located in its assigned location the warehouse multiple location for items consolidation in to as few location as possible by combining smaller. Don’t move, send or receive any material while your count is in progress containing it twice or missing it completely. Executing a physical Inventory A physical inventory process must be an independent position this means cannot be responsible for check in and receiving persons the committee member organized out of this responsibility persons it reduce /avoid the internal theft. Counting committee should not be given access to the inventory quantities recorded in the accounting record. This is called a blind count and helps to eliminate guessing on the part of counters as they would not know what the quantity is. Stop productionoperation (inventory transaction) on the day of counting or exercise proper control over movement of inventories. Do not make any movement of items either in to or out of the warehouse (even if they are misplaced). Do not fill orders or receives good during the count period there is a great risk of missing any items or there double count. • Proper control over count cards (tags) sheet is needed ensure that all cards sheets issued to counting member are sequentially numbered accounted for and returned after the counting process is finished including those which were voided or unused. • Immediately compare your counts with accounting records audit the counts and conducts recount if there are unacceptable differences. • Mark counted items and location. This should be to ensure inventory completeness i.e.no missing items or items counted twice which an important aspect of any physical inventory is. • When verifying your counts. Give special attention to fast moving and volume items such items usually have a greater risk of counting errors in comparing to slow moving items. Responsible committee member verifies that the counts in the warehouses are accurate the quantities can be entered in your computer. Find several counting errors in an area the entire section should be recounted. When verification is successfully completed all counts are entered in to the computer. 4 Analyzing Physical Inventory Result Analyzing the difference should estimate the effect they have on company process. Some of them may have little effect other may have significant effect and shows the areas where improvements are needed. Two methods of accuracy tracking are on hand –method & transactional method. In WFselect on-hand accuracy tracking methods this indicate percentage of error at concrete point of time in this methods accuracy tracking calculates Accuracy rate=Total difference amount(Shortage/Overage)X 100% On-hand inventory amount Transactional methods shows the accuracy of company operation it is a correlation of the difference amount and total consumed inventory amount during the period should be inventory accuracy is within 3% inventory management to be effective. To compare the result of previous physical counts for the reason of comparing current and last count results and seeing the effect of improvements in inventory management process. In the last carefully investigated the discrepancies need to make adjustments. Adjustment need to be made in the inventory listing. It should be useful for annual counting analyze the inventory count process in total and receive feedback from all department this feedback support for the next year count time updating inventory count policies and procedures. The committee member need to determine the source of discrepancies and then decide how to reduce them in the future let’s consider possible sources of difference.The company material properly controlled and uses. 5. Counting material Shortage ,overage, waste, damage or surplus During the counting period the company material will be happen material discrepancy this discrepancy identify where is the problem occurred, after the inventory finished the work has not stopped the assigned member several things to be address Overage/excess, shortage/missing, damage & wastage/surplus. • The committee member identifies any overage items discovered during the inventory recorded immediately. • The committee member identifies any shortage, damage items discovered during the inventory this items record separately by another form to inform immediately for management. The committee an informal investigation regarding the damaged or missing item. The basic who, what, when, where, and how should be explained. • If any damage items are economically repairable the committee member record and transfer to the responsible department for its repair. The materials not repair record and ready for disposal. 7-8 Disposal of Surplus, Scrap and Waste The final objective of inventory control is the detection of inactive stock items that may add to inventory investment without contributing any corresponding value. Inactive items may arise due to several factors such as:- • Over acquisition, over buying and over delivering • Change in design and specification • Abandonment of project or cancellation of contracts • Undetected errors in materials accounting • Error in record keeping or breakage Surpluses, scrap and waste have to be dispose. Disposal returns to avoiding either through discarding or selling the items with book value. Proper disposal of materials should be undertaken in conformance with the company policy and the dissection of committee member. The following alternative possibilities can be used for disposal of in active items. • Utilization /Cancelled from stock balance • Utilization by transfer to another project • Utilization by charge out/ discount on standard costs • Return to original supplier • Sales at book value on surplus scrap or salvage materials. 9-10 No further description is needed. • Supplementary Issues • Internal theft is a typical for retailers Good internal control is needed to prevent this issue in the future such internal control includes use of security cameras control over trash disposal. The stock control should be supervised and record carefully, the manager should be led by example and maintain appropriate discipline over recording the transaction. • Shop lifting Use of security cameras and sensor tags will be very helpful to significant reduces this problem. This problem occurred during any time to inform to police and record carefully. • Administrative error can be identified through comparison of the differences among location (maybe there is a shortage in one and the overage in another location at the same time) • Purchased material shipment a purchaser sends a shipment of inventory and indicates a quantity sent higher than what is actually in the shipment. In such cases the best control is to count all inventories received to ensure that the actual quantity matches the number provided by the vendor in the shipping documents 6. RISKS • Missing inventory schedules • Delay in schedule • Unexpected workload in respective departments • Disagreed departments and committees about the inventory schedule • Absence of personnel to be in a committee member • Shortage of finance • Improper preservation • Counting repeatedly • Miscounting / Double counting • Miss-registering of results • Errors when verifying results • Unclear results • Overlooking of discrepancies • Discussions for the action of discrepancies take too long • Disagreements when discussing the actions of discrepancies • Counting take too long • Improper record keeping 7. Related document…………………………10 FOR DOCUMENT CONTROL USE ONLY • PURPOSE The purpose of this procedure is to define the system to undertake the timely receipts, storage, upkeep, handling, accounting, issue and disposals of materials. 2. SCOPE The scope of this procedure applies to all materials managed at head office and at project level from material delivery up to material issued and accepts final report. 3. PROCESS OWNER Procurement& Supply Department Approved by: Signature: Date: 7/10/2020 Name: AmanuelTesfaye Designation: General Manager 4. DEFINITIONS 4.1DEFINITION Materials: are basic substances in its natural, modified, or semi processed state used as an input or to operations for subsequent modification or transformation into an output. Materials Management (MM):is the process of management which coordinates, supervises and executes the tasks associated with the flow of materials to, through, and out of an organization in an integrated fashion. Storehouse: a place where items are housed or a building designed for storage purposes and constructed with roof and complete side and end walls. Store management: it is a process of planning, coordination and control of various activities pertaining to efficient, effective and economic storage and store keeping. Inspection: to check all materials received. Storage: to keep everything in its proper place Issue: to issue materials and goods only when properly authorized. Store record: to maintain a correct record of any thing received or issued form store. Stock control: to arrange continuously receipts and issues to ensure that stock balances are sufficient, with due regard to economy. Stock verification: to physically verify the quantity and condition of goods lying in the store. Identification: to systematically define and describe all items in stock Stock accountant: the person recording stock movements and balances in value in computer and stock cards. Material handling means providing the right amount of the right material, in the right condition, at the right place, in the right position, in the right sequence, and for the right cost, by the right method(s). Receipt: receipt is the process of accepting from all sources, all materials, equipment and parts used in the company. Holding: although holding inventory results in additional cost it is necessary to maintain inventory to avoid running out of stock. 4.2. It is also responsible to notify all interested parties of arrival and condition of incoming material. It is at the receiving stage that the purchasing documents meet the physical materials. At this stage of material management functions the materials condition /status in critically examined to detect items which arrives detective, shortage in quantity, wrong shipment etc. and produce clerical report for immediate action. Any delays in this aspect mean a cost for the company. Receiving report produced Should be used • As a basis invoice payment • For continued purchasing negotiation • For closing the order Receiving Procedures • Unloading and checking the shipment • Unpacking and inspection the material • Completion of the receiving report • Delivery of the materials to requisitions 2 Identification The received goods should be identified by a clear way ofidentification. Without identification it is impossible to uniquely identify the materials needed. This problem can be solved using codification. The codification system applied both alphabetical & numerical systems. All material should be given a code identifying the material specifically, definitely, and unambiguously. Adopting a well-designed codification system enables the MMS/SK to have a unique, precise (i.e. exact), simple and consistent method of identifying stocks. Code should be compact, concise, and flexible enough to accommodate future addition. Coding of materials appropriately recorded in the user department and store to give the following advantage: • A large number of store items are reduced to smaller group of items in a systematic way. • It is easier for storing, recording and accounting to deal with categories or classes of materials rather than individual items. • Classification and codification helps easy location of stores. • Easy identification of store items facilitates prompt service. • Possibility of duplicate stock of the same item kept under a different name or description is avoided. • Long descriptions of materials are avoidance. Nomenclature of materials is simplified by choosing symbols& numbers which are simple, clear and free from duplication. • Systematic grouping helps in standardization of materials and encourages diverse uses of the same item. • It is useful for proper location of stores. It also forms a basis for setting up of different stores. The material items shall classified by: • Develop a unique identification method and describe A part from the above codification systems, a system by which the physical location of the items in the store should be identified. Each inventory items should be assigned as specific storage location. 3 Store Recording A good warehouse layout and good storage methods yield the following benefits • Ready accessibility of major materials. • Efficient space utilization and flexibility of arrangement. • A reduced need for materials handling equipment • Minimization of materials deterioration & pilferages • Ease of physical counting The first and foremost attention that should be given while storing of materials is to understand different information’s about the items to be stocked. All receipts, issues & transactions must continually and faithfully be recorded/ in bin cards. The balance shall be recorded immediately with the identification number, location and so on. • The company shallapply the following basic Principles of storage: • All the materials must be identified and coded. This helps in establishing their nature or identity. • Name, class and reference number should be recorded by each item of material. • To indicate the materials stored in bins, racks, shelves, etc. it must have signs or tags attached on them. • The storeroom should be divided into sections, and the materials/goods belonging to one class should be stored in each section. • In order to protect the materials from damage in storage, provision of proper storage space particular must be provided. • Floor plan showing the various section of storeroom should be posted indifferent parts of the storeroom. This helps eliminating wastage of time in the location of a particular material. • There must be a constant check on the balance on hand of quantities stored. Regular program of inspection, physical verification and maintenance of stores shall be in place. • Entry inside stores should be restricted. • No materials should be allowed to pass out from the stores, unless a written request of someone in authority is received. • Special attention must be given to perishable materials. Inflammable materials such as petrol, kerosene, oil, etc. should be stored in a place far away from the others items. • Oldest material should issue first. 4 Store Request Store Requisition (SR) Shall be Authorized by the User Department Head. Authorized SR shall be reviewed by the Store keeper to check and identify the stock level and stock balance .If the stock is available it shall be recorded in the Store Issue Voucherand dispatched fromstore. If the material is not available or not sufficient,Purchase Requisition (PR) will be prepared. No materials should be allowed to pass out from the stores, unless approved MaterialRequest is received. The purchase request must be authorized by the appropriate authority. The authority should see that the material requested is within the budget allocated tothe concerned department. Origination of Purchase Requisition (PR) Purchase Requisition is a document generated by the store that authorizes material purchase.The need for purchase originates in the MMS or in the User department. This need for purchase is transmitted to the ProcurementSection by approved Purchase Requisition. The Purchase Requisition is a serially numbered internal document by which the need for purchase is transmitted or communicated. 5. Issue and dispatch • SR approved by concerned authority, who decides the withdrawal of materials from the store shall be recorded properlyin Store IssueVouchers. The materials, withdrawn form a store have to be authorized. Only the requested quantity should be Issued • StoreIssue Voucher signed in appropriate form by individual who receive the material. 6 Selection of Fixed Asset Fixed Asset consists of all property owned by the company with a useful life of more than one year and a minimum cost of Br 1000 are categorized under this group. Items under 1000 Br are expensed automaticallyand registered by store section. *Items in the store that has fixed asset nature and not issued from the store until issued date should not be included in this category; rather they will be included as stock items. After the materials had been delivered, User Department shall be responsible for materials stored in their areas. The material delivered to users shall be used within a month, and it shall not be subjected to a high rate of deterioration or obsolescence Un used Materials shall be returned to store. To determine the actual usage of material during a given period, it is necessary to take a physical count of the material at the end of the period and to compare this figure with the similar beginning-period figures (which has been adjusted for materials receipts during the period). Hence, accounting changes are determined indirectly rather than directly. As a result, the system provides control over material usage only if it is used in conjunction with an accounting system employing standard cost techniques. 7 Report Finally the material issued from the warehouse the Store Keeper / MMS prepares the issued material quantity and amount depends on by Store Issue Voucher. These reports prepared daily and summarize Monthly. they finally prepared and approved by concerned body and send the report to PSD. 5.3 Supplementary Issues • Bin Card: - Cards which shows the receipt, issuer, stock balance and location of the items record by store keeper code settles ware house. • Stock Card: - Cards which shows the receipt, issue, unit price, stock balance, total price the same us to bin cards this card recorded by stock Clark/ stock account. The balance should be equal to the bin card. • GoodsReceiving Voucher (GRV): - This is a receiving pad recorded by store keeper/ stock Clark all requested question fulfills and distribute the GRN immediately the material received after that distribution. • Material request: - This pad prepares by user department. PS/Purchaser 5.2 Description of process steps FLW Description 1 PS, Purchaser shall receive the Approved Purchase Request and consult with the user Department Head / PSD to proceed with the purchasing process. 2 PSD Head or the General Manager make theDecision on the purchasing of Local or foreign market. 3 Verification of Authority and Budget The responsibility of the Materials Management Section or user department is to give details of items with full descriptions. However, the responsibility of the PSD is to check whether the PR is within the budget limit or not and also checking the accuracy of the document. Budget reference number writes in the purchase requisition. 4,5 Request for Quotation or Bids /Price Quotation/ This refers to identification and analysis of possible sources of supply. A Quotation is a statement (Performa) acquired from potential suppliers. Requests for Quotation are a process of initiating potential suppliers that are willing to compete to supply the required material. There are two types of Bids: Open Bid– It is a type of bid where all potential suppliers are invited through mass media and advertising agents to participate in the bidding. Closed Bid– In this case selected suppliers are approached (invited) to participate in the bid. Here, the invitation can be made through personal contact, telephone or formal letter. Issuing of Enquires and Tender Collection In the case of closed bid the company use letters or printed enquiry form because it knows the bidder. But in the case of Open tender, the company use mass media. Preparation of the tender involves: • Bidding Notice • Bidder’s instruction • Description of Materials • Samples and blue prints (when required) • Tender Documents In order to give general description of the materials; delivery time and point, term of payment, last date of submitting bids, general term and condition should be included. In the process of collecting tenders the company need to set up separate boxes & seal the boxes on the due date & time. After collecting the tender, the company needs to open the tender. Tender opening involves the following activities. • Earnest money deposit • Time, date & place should be specified • If the service or material needs special expertise or professionalism, virtual/technical team will be assigned. • In normal bidder selection when the money is below 100,000.00 the purchasing committee will open the tender. These and other things should enter the tender opening register or minute. The minute should contain price, delivery date, discount, delivery point, & others if any. Here suppliers that do not pay bid bonds should get back their letters unopened and bid letters arriving between the closing date and the opening date should also be returned to the supplier unopened. • Note: on some cases potential suppliers will be contacted directly and the purchasing will be executed with them. 6 Opening Of Performa Invoice The request depends on the type of materials because some materials need price quotations and other not in the company items that have less than 5,000 birr value purchase directly without quotation; and 5001-50,000birr need Performa invoice. Above 100,001 birr the notice should be advertised on mass media as newspapers ,collected Performa opens by purchase committee member all purchases opened by purchase committee opened Performa approved by General Manager or assigned person. 7 Sample Approval The requested material specifications Prepared and material quality approved by user department by using sample or by visiting supplier’s premises. 8,9 Evaluation of Bids & Selection of Suppliers This is analysis of the potential suppler who fulfill the criteria of the company. Suppliers are evaluated /reviewed by the following factors or selection criteria. ► In terms of price proposed by the suppliers. ► In terms of discount they offer. ► In terms of the shipping terms ► In terms of delivery date ► In terms of reliability of the supplier by analyzing past performance ► In terms of reciprocity (this refers to mutual interchange of favors, privileges in good sense) ► In terms of quality of work & other services Here the lowest bidder usually wins the tender, but sometimes this bidder may be denied or not awarded to supply. This happens because of the following reasons; • A higher bidder may provide better after sale service. • A higher bidder may have better plant facilities and be able to offer quality provided than the low bidder. • The low bidder may not be reliable. • The reciprocity may favor some company other than the low bidder. • The low bidder may be located so far from the company. • Exceptional goodwill may exist between higher bidder & the buyer. • The company may adhere to the policy of dealing with local suppliers. Local Purchase Evaluation Sheet • After the opening of Performa invoice purchase evaluation sheet prepared by PS/Purchaser. • Purchase evaluation sheet is verified by PSD and finally approved by GM. 10,11 Issuing of Purchase Order The Purchase Requisition gives the purchaser to order the materials described in the requisitions. The Procurement Section / Purchaser should maintain or have access to an up-to-date list of vendors, which includes price, available discounts, estimated delivery time, and any other relevant information. From this list, the Purchasing Section / Purchaser selects a vender from whom high quality materials can be obtained when needed at competitive cost is selected. Then the purchaser completes a Purchase Order, which is a purchasing document that formalizes a purchase transaction with the seller. So a Purchase Order is a serially numbered document that is used to make purchases. The Purchase Order should contain the following information. • Suppliers name and address. • Quotation reference and date. • Description of items. • Quantity Ordered. • Unit Price. • Terms of Payment. • Date of the order. • Delivery date and • Signature of the purchasing agent Issue Payment Request After approval of evaluation sheet & signed contract agreements to request the payment from finance department. Payment Request • Payment request requested by purchase officer. • Payment request finally approved by GM. 12 Follow-up and expediting the Order Follow-up refers to reminding the supplier to insure the timely arrival of the Order. And expediting is speeding up or accelerating the receipt of the item before the agreed-up on time. The later requires good relationship between the company & supplier. In WF, we will use manually & computerized systems. Manually system is a calendar follow up system. This is keeping the follow up order on the required date when the next follow up is scheduled or suppliers list.This is filling order alphabetically on the top we are going to use a number running from 1 to 30/31 and put a visible colored mark on the date the next follow up is made. 13 Receiving, Inspecting and Storing When the items are received, the following receiving procedures are usually adopted. • Unpacking and checking the material – Compare for the right material that the packing ship contains with the materials received. Here, we need to check for the right quantity and General Condition of the material. • Completing the receiving report and distribute this report to: • Delivery of materials: these materials may be delivered to the user department or to the Store. Finally, whoever is received the material will sign on the receiving report. Inspection Report: Whenever it is necessary to take technical inspection, we may make sample/all inspection. This depends on the nature of material and/or on the description of those materials. Based on this technical report, if the material is not useful (partly or wholly) the purchasing people will notify the supplier how to handle those items. In this case the possible courses of action would be: 1. Return the material to the supplier. 2. Keep some of the more acceptable material and return the rest. 3. Keep all and rework it to the point where it is acceptable. When is Inspection Justified? This depends on economies of scale, which is based on two basic costs. i. Cost of Inspection ii. Costs resulting from defectiveness entering the production operation and/or reaching customers. 14 Closing the Order After making the necessary payment to the vendor, closing an order simply entails a consolidation of all documents and correspondence relevant to the order in filling them in closed order file which include a purchase requisition, the open order file of the purchase order, the acknowledgement, the receiving report, the inspection report and any note or correspondence pertaining to the order. 15 The PSD, PS/Purchaser shall open foreign purchase operation 16, 17 The PS/Purchasershall collect Proforma and Select the collected Proforma with PSD and get approval from GM 18 PS/Purchaser has responsibility to order purchase. 19 Purchaser shall start the banking process and follow up till the purchased materials delivered. 5.3. Supplementary Issues 5.3.1. Important Issues in Purchasing i. Make or Buy decision ii. Organization of Purchasing a. Centralized Purchasing This occurs when the authority and responsibility to handle the material needs of the company is given to one department. b. Decentralized Purchasing This is to apply the project purchaser to purchase the material items of low value and of routine use are purchased under decentralization. C. Computerized Purchasing This occurs when both the centralized and decentralized purchasing are operated in a company. Items of high value and those that require high technical analysis and knowledge of experts are purchased under centralized purchasing. 5.3.2 Type of Purchasing This is the right time aspect of purchasing. The quality of materials affects the price and time of purchase. The company should have time of purchase for their construction process, because materials could have increase/decrease in price seasonably depending on the circumstances. Here based on time dimension, there are four time-based types of purchasing. These are • Hand to mouth • Current Requirement • Forward buying • Speculative buying 5.3.3. Discounts in Purchasing The other important factor which can influence the Procurement Section / Purchaser insuppler selection or tender evaluation is discount. A discount is a reduction allowed by a seller to a purchasing department by the following discount methods i. Cash Discount ii. Quantity Discounts iii. Trade Discounts 6. RISKS • Unclear/Incorrect purchasing information • Reviews and Approvals take too long • Collecting Proforma take too long • Lack of updated supplier list • Biased evaluation • Lack of required material in the market • Miscounting of materials • Typing error • Ambiguity of contracts • Sellers may not supply as per the prior contractual agreement & specifications or may supply low quality products. • Goods in-transit may be lost, destroyed by fire, damaged due to different reasons. • The supplier may deliver products that reach its expiry date • Delay of payments • Overlooking insignificant non-conformities of purchased materials when inspecting • Delay of delivery 7. RECORDS • Purchase Request Records • Material Request • Good Receiving Voucher • Supplier list • Supplier performance evaluation • Performa different supplier record • Purchase order • Evaluation record • Request for quotation • Purchase committee minute 8. SCOPE The procedure covers all activities for planning, conducting customer satisfaction, monitoring and reporting the results PROCESS OWNER Marketing & Sales Department, MR Approved by:Signature:Date: 7/10/2020 Name: Amanuel Tesfaye Designation: General Manager 4. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.1 Definitions For the purpose of this procedure the following definitions and the definitions given on ISO 9000:2015 apply. Customers Satisfaction Customer’s perception of the degree as to whether the WF has met customer requirements Realization: Need or exception that is stated, generally implied or obligator NOTE 1: Generally implied means that it is custom or common practice for the WF, its customers and other and other interested parties, that the need or expectation under consideration is implied. Requirement: - Need or Expectation that is stated, generally implied or obligatory. Quality: - degree to which a state of inherent characteristics fulfils requirement. 4.2 Abbreviations MR: Management Representative QMS: Quality Management System OD: Operation Department MSD: Marketing & Sales Department FLW: Flowchart OP: Operating Procedure WI: Work Instruction OF: Operating Form EX: External Document WF: Waterfit General Trading 5. PROCEDURE 5.1 Process FLW Input Process Out put Responsibility 1. Monitoring plan Customer Order Registration Logbook 2. Identified customer 3. Customer satisfaction survey questionnaires 4. Gathered Information Appropriate statistical tool (s) 5.Organized and Analyzed Information 6.Customer Satisfaction Draft Report 7. Approved Customer Satisfaction Report 1. Identified Customer 2. Determined Methods(S) 3.Collected Information 4.Organized and Analyzed information 5.Customer Satisfaction Draft Report 6. Approved Customer Satisfaction Report 7.Initiated corrective Action 1. MR and MSD 2. MR and MSD 3. Assigned Expert 4. MR and MSD 5.MR and MSD 6. GM, Top management 7.MR 5.2. Process Step Description FLW Process Step 1 Identifying & Listing Customers Customer satisfaction monitoring plan is prepared by MR & MSD to monitor information relating to customer perception as to whether the organization has met customer requirements. The plan is periodically adjusted to account for the status and importance of customer satisfaction with respect to particular aspects and availability of the information and methods for collecting it. Customer satisfaction monitoring should be conducted at least once per year. Based on customer satisfaction monitoring plan MR and MSD are responsible for identifying & listing immediate customers i.e. customers with whom there is direct contractual relationship from customer Order Registration Logbook. The ultimate customers/the final service users having no direct contractual relationship can also be considered. 2 Determine feedback monitoring method MR and MSD should determine the methods(S) of monitoring & using information relating to customer perception as to whether the organization has met customer requirements. Measures such as service quality requirement, delivery, price, etc. Should also be determined. The focus areas, scope, resources and program for collecting customer satisfaction information should also be determined. Information on customer satisfaction are acquired from customer feedback and by analyzing customer behavior through on or more of the following ways: Scheduled customer satisfaction survey questionnaires, sent directly to customers covering service aspects that are relevant to customer satisfaction such as; Adequacy of product’s functional, performance and other design features Packaging & labeling Delivery performance against schedule Product information Availability Sales and order processing After sales support and service Price etc Focus group meetings within the customer’s organization such as with top management, marketing, purchasing and quality assurance through conferences or organized events/ forums such as customer day, etc; Monitoring customer complaints such as overall number of complaints, the up/downward trends, and distribution of complaints by type of customer, location as well as nature of complaint covering all service scopes, warranty, after sales support etc. Monitoring data recorded from routine calls from departments and services, and Any other method determined by top management. 3 Collecting information and feedback The assigned expert/staff should collect information and feedback regarding customer satisfaction through customer satisfaction Survey Questionnaires or focus group meeting with customers. Data on customer complaints is obtained from the complaints handling record. 4 Organizing & analysis of information All collected information and feedback regarding customer satisfaction through customer survey, analyzing customer complaints, focus group meeting outcomes or other means indicating the level of customer satisfaction are analyzed using appropriate statistical tools 5 Reporting customers satisfaction monitoring results Results of the analysis indicating the scope of the assessment, attained customer satisfaction levels in all customer categories, statistical measures indicating capability to meet customer requirements, comparisons with results from previous times if any, etc. are complied into Customer Satisfaction Report, to be presented to top management for management review according to Management review procedure. 6. RISKS Lack of updated list of customers Unregistered customers on the log book Defined method not fit all the customers Unwilling customer to give information/feedback Data collection take too long Misunderstood information/feedback Unclear questioners Analysis & Report writing take too long Disagreements with the respective departments on the feedbacks Reviews & Approvals take too long Customer may forgot on customer identifying list Wrong feedback Customer satisfaction report may not enclosed all the feedbacks Unrelated resolutions given Corrective actions take too long 7. RECORDS Customer satisfaction monitoring report Management review Minutes Reports of actions taken on customer satisfaction monitoring findings. 8. SCOPE This procedure is applicable to all welding processes PROCESS OWNER Operation Department, Welding Section, Project Managers Approved by:Signature:Date: 7/10/2020 Name: Amanuel TesfayeDesignation: General Manager DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.1 Definitions For the purpose of this document in addition to the definitions given in ISO 9000:2015, the following definitions apply. Butt Welding: It is a welding technique used to connect parts which are nearly parallel and don’t overlap. 4.2 Abbreviations WF: Waterfit General Trading GM: General Manager MR: Management Representative OD: Operation Department OP: Operational Procedure OF: Operational Form FLW: Flowchart PROCEDURE INPUT FLW OUTPUT RESPONSIBILITY Contract agreement Work order Operational Plan Resource request or plan Environmental scanning Welding Preparation Alignment of pipes Shave Surface Checked the pipes alignment No Yes Work order Operational plan Resource request or plan Environmental scanning Welding Preparation Alignment of pipes Shave the Surface Checked the pipes alignment Cleaning pipe Job owner Process Owners Process owner/ Assigned person Process owner/ Assigned person Dep’t Heads, Process Owners Process owner/ Assigned person Process owner/ Assigned person Process owner/ Assigned person Process owner/ Assigned person 5.1 Flowchart Cleaning pipe Heated surface Fusion surface Cooling time Confirmed Welded seam Heated surface Fusion surface Cooling time Confirmed Welded seam Welded pipe Process owner/ Assigned person Process owner/ Assigned person Process owner/ Assigned Dep’t Heads, Process Owners Dep’t Heads, Process Owners 5.2 Description of Processes FLW Process Steps The job owner receive work order or contract specification The process owner shall prepare plan for the operation The process owner or the assigned person shall ensure all the resources needed to meet the objective and deadline of the work are avail. The process owner or the assigned person shall ensure the suitability of environment for the welding. If it is not suitable, wait for the suitable time and conditions. The welding zone must be protected from unsuitable weather conditions (e.g. humidity effects, wind and temperatures below 0°C). The surfaces to be joined must be undamaged and free from impurities or loose particles. The Department Heads or Process Owners shall prepare the machines which are needed for the operation The pipes must be aligned when they are clamped into the mirror welder in such a way that the surfaces are in the same plane (parallel) to each other. The HDPE pipes can be positioned directly into the welding machine. Install the correct adapter insert for the size of pipe diameter to be used and tighten them to the machine. Position the pipe in a way that approx. 40mm is protruding behind the last clamp. By doing this, you will have approx. 10 to 15mm to shave from, and the remaining 25 to 30 mm should be sufficient for welding. Once the pipe has been placed in position, the top clamps can be closed. It is important to tighten the top clamp nuts evenly in order to get a totally circular pipe, an even clamping pressure must be achieved. Then, make the first dry matching (press the two pipes to each other) and check the amount of shaving that will be required. After the dry matching is completed, open up the pipes and introduce the shaver. Turn the shaver on and adjust to suitable speed. Press the two pipes together, and shave until a continuous strip of HDPE is peeling off on both sides of the shaver. Once constant peeling off is observed, release the pressure on the pipes and separate the pipes. Do not turn off the shaver until the pipes are apart. If the shaver is stopped during shaving, the shaver will create an end cut-mark and the shaving operation will have to be repeated. Remove the shaver, match the pipes again, and check the pipe for proper alignment. Sometimes, even when continuous peeling off is achieved on each side of the shaver, the pipes do not match properly. This is normally due to the clamps, which are pressing on to the pipe with different pressures. Re-tightening the nuts slightly on either side is one solution. But, if this does not help, shimming normally does the job. Open up one clamp and insert a shim in between the jaws and the pipe. This shim will concentrate the pressure on to the pipe and move the pipe into alignment. It is important to remember that, if the clamp has been opened during operation, the shaving operation must be repeated. Once the pipes are correctly aligned, separate the pipes again for cleaning. Remove chips inside the pipes on both sides, all chips scattered under the pipes, and also inside the machine. Otherwise, they will stick to the mirror (heat plate) later while re-heating. Remove the chips by using a brush or a small hook made out of a thin steel wire. Never put any dirty gloves inside the pipe or remove the chips with your hands. Do not touch the shaved pipe ends. To be on the safe side, always clean the surface with a clean rag and mineral spirits/alcohol before you introduce the mirror. Before you introduce the mirror, you should have all parameters available for this operation. Also check the mirror temperature. Normally, the mirror has a yellow or red lamp, which tells you if the mirror has reached working temperature. To make sure there is no cold air flowing through the pipe, place some plastic bags on each end of the pipe, this will prevent the air from cooling the mirror on one side. You have now shaved the pipe into a good fit and removed the shaver and introduced the mirror. Push the pipes together against the mirror and raise the pressure to the Bead-up pressure. This pressure needs to be maintained until the Bead-up height has been reached. The bead up height is the height of the bead, which is pressing up against the mirror. As soon as the Bead up height has been reached, release the pressure down to the Heat Soak pressure. Heat soak pressure is the pressure maintained during the Heat Soak time. As soon as the heat soak time has elapsed, separate the pipes, remove the mirror, and then press together. This operation has to be done quite fast, since there is actually a time limit “Transfer time” from the removal of the mirror until the two pipes are pressed together and reached the Fusion pressure. Fusion pressure is the pressure that shall reach during the Transfer time and maintained during the Cooling time. Cooling time is the time in which the pipe has to be left undisturbed. Under no circumstances shall the clamps be opened or the pressure released until the cooling time has elapsed. The mirror-welding machine, if coupled to a data log, will give a print -out confirming the parameters used during welding of a specific seam and approval/rejection of the welded seam. If the specific seam gets approval the welded pipes will hand over to the customers. 6. RISKS 7. RECORDS The following records shall be maintained: 8. COMPLIANCE 5 Approved by: Signature: Date: 7/10/2020 Name: Amanuel Tesfaye Designation: General Manager INTRODUCTION Water Fit General Trading is committed to protect and safeguard its people and stakeholders by creating safe & healthy working environment. In line with the WHO & Ethiopian Ministry of Health Guiding Principles on Covid-19 Pandemic prevention & Response, WF recognizes the corporate responsibility to comply and commit to prevent the life of its people. POLICYOBJECTIVES The objective of this Water Fit’s Health & Safety Policy is to provide a direction & a guideline for its employees and business partners about the COVID-19 Pandemic Prevention & Response. POLICY SCOPE WF’s Health & Safety Policy applies to all employees, anyone doing business for or with WF and others acting on WF’s behalf. This applies to all locations where WF conducts business and to all company-sponsored events. DEFINITIONS COVID-19 Pandemic: an infectious disease caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome corona virus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). It was first identified in December 2019 in Wuhan, Hubei, China, and has resulted in an ongoing pandemic. Health & Safety: an organization's statement regarding its commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy work environment. ABBREVIATIONS WF: Water Fit General Trading PO: Policy GUIDELINES Based on the international & national Health & Safety guidelines on Covid-19 prevention & Response, the following guidelines shall be applied in WF: Prevention precautions at work places Employees are obligated to follow the general hygiene rules, such as: Wash your hands after using the toilet, before eating, and if you cough/sneeze into your hands (follow the 20-second hand-washing rule). You can also use the sanitizers you’ll find around the office. Cough/sneeze into your sleeve, preferably into your elbow. If you use a tissue, discard it properly and clean/sanitize your hands immediately. Open the windows regularly to ensure open ventilation. Avoid touching your face, particularly eyes, nose, and mouth with your hands to prevent from getting infected. If you find yourself coughing/sneezing on a regular basis, avoid close physical contact with your coworkers and take extra precautionary measures (such as requesting sick leave). Clean your machineries and tools after using. Screening All employees’ and visitors’ Temperature shall be screened at the gate. If the temperature is above the normal state, it should be reported to the office and the employee &/or the visitor shall not be entered the premises Using Personal Protective Equipments (PPE), Disinfectants &Cleaning Responsibilities All employees should wear face masks when entered the premises and during works. Keep your masks and other protection materials clean at all times By using the available disinfectant clean your work station. Use only your PPE for yourself and always keep it clean. Infection control responses If any employee has cold symptoms, such as cough/sneezing/fever, or feels poorly, request sick leave or work from home. If any employee has a positive COVID-19 diagnosis, they can return to the office only after they’ve fully recovered, with a doctor’s note confirming your recovery. Work sites & Work hour arrangements By following the government’s regulations and directives, working hours shall be arranged to avoid and minimize social contacting and movements in the city. The arrangements shall be communicated to all employees and stakeholders accordingly. Travel Restrictions All work trips and events – both domestic and international – will be cancelled/postponed until further notice. In-person meetings should be done with a careful distancing and ventilated room. If you normally commute to the office by public transportation and do not have other alternatives, it should be done with a careful distancing and prevention. If you are planning to travel voluntarily to a high-risk city with increased COVID-19 cases, we’ll ask you to work from home for 14 calendar days. You will also be asked not to come into physical contact with any colleagues during this time. Risk identification &mitigation resources WF shall always follow the data released by the Ministry of Health to identify risks per zones and plan the mitigation accordingly. System for tracking cases & consultation for emergency response The first-line emergency response contacts for consultation and tracking cases shall be available. Healthcare services WF will follow its employees’ healthcare protocol to handle healthcare during this pandemic. Communication means & levels (Internal & External) All employees shall communicate their concerns, information and questions to their immediate supervisors or to the respective department heads. Communicating external stakeholders shall be handled by respective departments and the general manager. Information sources The information source shall always be from the government authorities’ regulations & directives and WHO directives. Awareness/induction to employees the policy and response plan This policy shall be communicated to all employees in an effective manner. RESPONSIBILITY The Health & Safety policy is owned and maintained by all departments and functions in WF. Top Management is responsible for the creation, administration, updating and communication of the policy. 0COMPLIANCE Employees and all stakeholders are expected to comply with this and all applicable WF policies. Violation of this policy or the refusal to cooperate will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination and referral to the appropriate authorities.
